=============================================================================
 SCOPE OF THIS REWRITE
=============================================================================
 This notebook is the Chapter-4 companion to hmm_training_tesi.Rmd. It was
 rewritten to match the decisions taken for Chapter 3 and Chapter 4:

   * NO TRAIN/TEST SPLIT anywhere. The bundle no longer carries `test_data`
     and every held-out / out-of-sample analysis has been deleted, including
     the old Section 1 (decode test patients) and Section 2.10 (validation
     against held-out Viterbi).
   * The day-7 DEPTH anchor (old Section 3bis) has been deleted in full,
     together with everything cascading from it (3bis.6, the three-anchor
     comparison of 3ter.5, the day-7 depth KM stratum).
   * DD-plots (old 2.7) and the breakdown-point simulation (old 2.8) have
     been deleted in full.
   * STAYER_WINDOW is fixed at 14 (the whole grid), so the stayer/switcher
     split reproduces Chapter 3 exactly: 887 stayers / 152 switchers.

 Two branches survive and only these two propagate downstream:
   (A) the ADMISSION anchor  — depth phenotype from the day-0 vector alone;
   (B) the DAY-7 ONLINE anchor — Viterbi on the panel truncated to 0..7.
 (B) is leak-free IN TIME, not in patients. It must never be described as
 out-of-sample.

 Chapter 4 section map (the numbering below mirrors the chapter):
   1 -> 4.1 State-occupancy patterns: stayers and switchers
   2 -> 4.2 Admission phenotypes from statistical depth

# 0. Setup

This notebook depends on the fitted-model bundle written by
`hmm_training_tesi.Rmd` in its Section 12. Run that notebook first.

**Scope**: post-hoc analyses for the **covariate-free** HMM. Covariates
never enter the HMM; they appear here only as descriptors and as
adjustment terms in the outcome models of Sections 4 and 6.

## 0.1 Configuration

```{r config}
# ── Bundle ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The training notebook writes hmm_fit_objects_tesi4.rds. The first existing
# path wins, so older bundle names still work without editing this chunk.
BUNDLE_CANDIDATES <- c("hmm_fit_objects_tesi4.rds")
BUNDLE_PATH <- BUNDLE_CANDIDATES[file.exists(BUNDLE_CANDIDATES)][1]
stopifnot(!is.na(BUNDLE_PATH))

# ── Output directory for figures and tables ─────────────────────────────────
FIG_DIR <- "figures_ch4"
TAB_DIR <- "tables_ch4"

# ── Stayer definition ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# FIXED at 14, i.e. the whole observation grid (days 0..14). A patient is a
# stayer iff the globally decoded state is constant over the entire window,
# which is the definition |S_i| = 1 fixed in Chapter 3. Do NOT change this:
# any other value desynchronises every count in this notebook from
# Chapter 3's Table "Stayers by state" (887 / 152, split 273/233/207/174).
STAYER_WINDOW <- 14L

# ── Depth-based "central population" cut (Section 2) ─────────────────────────
# Fraction of the post-outlier population retained as the central core of each
# state. Two-step filter: drop depth = 0 (outside the convex hull), then keep
# the deepest CENTRAL_FRAC fraction. CENTRAL_FRAC = 1 disables the second step.
CENTRAL_FRAC <- 0.50

# Warn-flag threshold on the max-across-states depth of a classified patient.
# Patients below it are flagged as atypical but still assigned.
OUTLIER_DEPTH_THRESHOLD <- 1e-3

# ── Checkpoints ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Occupancy alluvial (Section 1): the three checkpoints used in the thesis
# figure. Switcher alluvial (Section 6.1): a finer grid.
OCCUPANCY_CHECKPOINTS <- c(0L, 7L, 14L)
SWITCHER_CHECKPOINTS  <- c(0L, 3L, 7L, 10L, 14L)
MIN_TRAJECTORY_FREQ   <- -1      # no filtering of rare sequences

# ── Anchors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DAY_TARGET is the clinical decision day requested by the ward. It defines
# the ONLINE decoding anchor (Section 3) and the first alert window
# (Section 6). There is no day-7 DEPTH anchor any more.
DAY_TARGET <- 7L

# ── Outcomes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#   discharge_dead           — in-hospital death (1) vs discharged alive (0)
#   discharge_mortality_90d  — death within 90 days of admission_end_date
OUTCOME_COLS        <- c("discharge_dead", "discharge_mortality_90d")
TRAJECTORY_OUTCOMES <- c("discharge_dead", "discharge_mortality_90d")

# ── Reference state for every logistic / KM model ────────────────────────────
# "Stable" is the interpretable baseline and matches the Chapter 3 ordering.
REF_STATE <- "Stable"

# ── Adjustment set: what the clinician knows at the bedside on day zero ─────
# Admission-time only. LOS is deliberately EXCLUDED: it is measured after
# admission and lies on the path from state to death, so conditioning on it
# induces collider bias. admission_infection is derived from the
# admission_reason field in Section 4.0 and is therefore not a df_full column.
ADJUST_COVARS <- c("age", "sex", "Barthel_index", "CIRS_total_score",
                   "admission_infection")

# ── Analysis plan ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One primary analysis is declared in advance; everything else is secondary or
# sensitivity. In-hospital death is a bounded binary outcome and is modelled by
# logistic regression. 90-day mortality is a time-to-event outcome and is
# modelled by Cox regression anchored at ADMISSION, so that in-hospital deaths
# are events rather than exclusions.
PRIMARY_ANCHOR   <- "admission"
BOOT_B           <- 300L    # bootstrap replicates for optimism correction
BOOT_SEED        <- 20260916L

# ── Death-aware truncation (Section 6.1) ─────────────────────────────────────
IS_DEAD_COL <- "is_dead"

# ── Survival analysis ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# days_death_from_discharge encoding (stage 2, two-sentinel scheme):
#   >= 1  → days between admission_end_date and death (event observed)
#   -1    → alive at end of follow-up (censored)
#   -2    → died IN-HOSPITAL; post-discharge survival undefined, excluded
# Time origin of the primary analysis is the DISCHARGE date.
DATE_OF_DEATH_COL     <- "days_death_from_discharge"
ADMISSION_DEATH_COL   <- "days_death_from_admission"
SURVIVAL_FOLLOWUP     <- 90L

# ── Alert system (Section 6) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Clinically driven: the ward asked for model-based support around day 7.
# First check at day 7 against baseline (day 0); later checks every two days
# against the state two days earlier.
ALERT_CHECK_DAYS <- c( 7L,  9L, 11L, 13L)
ALERT_PREV_DAYS  <- c( 0L,  7L,  9L, 11L)

# Stratification of alerted patients
STRAT_CONTINUOUS  <- c("Barthel_index", "Braden_score", "age",
                       "CIRS_total_score", "length_of_stay_days",
                       "count_admission_reasons")
STRAT_CATEGORICAL <- c("sex", "ECOG", "solid_tumor_category",
                       "discharge_dead", "discharge_mortality_90d",
                       "admission_infection")
STRAT_FOCUS       <- c("Barthel_index", "Braden_score", "CIRS_total_score",
                       "count_admission_reasons")
STRAT_FOCUS_CAT   <- c("discharge_dead", "admission_infection")

# Multiplicity control across the stratification tests
P_ADJUST_METHOD <- "BH"

# Permutation negative control for the alert (Section 6.6)
PERM_B    <- 2000L
PERM_SEED <- 41703192L

# Admission-reason code marking infection (token-exact match on a
# pipe-separated field, e.g. "1 | 4 | 10").
INFECTION_CODE <- "1"
```

## 0.3 Figure and table export helpers

Every figure and table that Chapter 4 could plausibly use is written to
disk, so the thesis includes artefacts produced by this run rather than
screenshots. Naming follows the Chapter 3 convention.

```{r export-helpers}
dir.create(FIG_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(TAB_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Save a ggplot / patchwork object as PNG (screen) and PDF (LaTeX).
save_fig <- function(plot, name, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300) {
  png_path <- file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".png"))
  pdf_path <- file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".pdf"))
  ok <- tryCatch({
    ggplot2::ggsave(png_path, plot = plot, width = width, height = height,
                    dpi = dpi, bg = "white")
    TRUE
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("[figure FAILED] ", name, " (png): ", conditionMessage(e), "\n", sep = "")
    FALSE
  })
  # The PDF is the file LaTeX includes. cairo_pdf gives better font handling
  # but is not present in every R build, so fall back to the default device.
  tryCatch(
    ggplot2::ggsave(pdf_path, plot = plot, width = width, height = height,
                    device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, bg = "white"),
    error = function(e)
      tryCatch(ggplot2::ggsave(pdf_path, plot = plot, width = width,
                               height = height, bg = "white"),
               error = function(e2)
                 cat("[figure FAILED] ", name, " (pdf): ",
                     conditionMessage(e2), "\n", sep = "")))
  if (ok) cat("[figure] ", png_path, "\n", sep = "")
  invisible(ok)
}

# Save a BASE-GRAPHICS figure (bagplots). `expr` is re-evaluated once per
# device, so it must be a self-contained drawing expression.
save_base_fig <- function(expr, name, width = 10, height = 8, res = 300) {
  e <- substitute(expr)
  png_path <- file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".png"))
  pdf_path <- file.path(FIG_DIR, paste0(name, ".pdf"))
  ok <- tryCatch({
    grDevices::png(png_path, width = width, height = height, units = "in",
                   res = res, bg = "white")
    eval(e, envir = parent.frame()); grDevices::dev.off()
    grDevices::pdf(pdf_path, width = width, height = height, bg = "white")
    eval(e, envir = parent.frame()); grDevices::dev.off()
    TRUE
  }, error = function(err) {
    while (grDevices::dev.cur() > 1) grDevices::dev.off()
    cat("[figure FAILED] ", name, ": ", conditionMessage(err), "\n", sep = "")
    FALSE
  })
  if (ok) cat("[figure] ", png_path, "\n", sep = "")
  invisible(ok)
}

# ggsurvplot objects are lists, not ggplots: arrange them first so the risk
# table is kept. Falls back to the curve panel alone if arranging fails.
save_km_fig <- function(gs, name, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300) {
  obj <- tryCatch(
    survminer::arrange_ggsurvplots(list(gs), print = FALSE, ncol = 1, nrow = 1),
    error = function(e) gs$plot)
  save_fig(obj, name, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi)
}

# Save a data frame as CSV and echo it as a kable.
save_tab <- function(df, name, caption = NULL, digits = 3) {
  path <- file.path(TAB_DIR, paste0(name, ".csv"))
  utils::write.csv(df, path, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("[table] ", path, "\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(df, digits = digits, caption = caption, row.names = FALSE))
  invisible(df)
}
```

## 0.4 Load fitted-model bundle

```{r load-bundle}
bundle   <- readRDS(BUNDLE_PATH)

hmm      <- bundle$hmm
hmm_data <- bundle$hmm_data
df_full  <- bundle$df_full

# Hard stop if a legacy bundle still carries a held-out partition: there is no
# train/test split anywhere in this thesis, and silently ignoring one would
# leave the cohort sizes inconsistent with Chapters 1 and 3.
if (!is.null(bundle$test_data) && nrow(bundle$test_data) > 0)
  stop("Bundle carries a non-empty test_data. Re-run hmm_training_tesi.Rmd ",
       "with TEST_FRAC = 0; this notebook has no held-out branch.")
if (!is.null(bundle$test_ids) && length(bundle$test_ids) > 0)
  stop("Bundle carries test_ids. Re-run the training notebook with TEST_FRAC = 0.")

# ── Compatibility: derive discharge_dead if the bundle predates the rename ───
if (!"discharge_dead" %in% names(df_full) && "discharged_alive" %in% names(df_full)) {
  df_full$discharge_dead <- 1L - as.integer(as.character(df_full$discharged_alive))
  cat("Derived discharge_dead = 1 - discharged_alive.\n")
}

N_STATES           <- bundle$config$N_STATES
RESPONSE_VARS      <- bundle$config$RESPONSE_VARS
RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE <- bundle$config$RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE
OBS_COVARIATES     <- bundle$config$OBS_COVARIATES
APPLY_ZSCORE       <- bundle$config$APPLY_ZSCORE
IS_a_MVN           <- bundle$config$IS_a_MVN
display_to_safe    <- bundle$name_map$display_to_safe
safe_to_display    <- bundle$name_map$safe_to_display
needs_expm1        <- bundle$needs_expm1
zscore_params      <- bundle$zscore_params

display     <- function(s)  unname(safe_to_display[s])
display_vec <- function(s)  unname(safe_to_display[s])

# ── Clinical state remap ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!is.null(bundle$state_remap) && !is.null(bundle$state_levels)) {
  state_remap     <- bundle$state_remap
  state_remap_inv <- bundle$state_remap_inv
  state_levels    <- bundle$state_levels
  state_colours   <- bundle$state_colours
} else {
  state_remap     <- seq_len(N_STATES)
  state_remap_inv <- seq_len(N_STATES)
  state_levels    <- paste0("State ", seq_len(N_STATES))
  state_colours   <- setNames(bundle$state_palette, state_levels)
}
pal <- unname(state_colours)

# Reference state used by every model in this notebook.
if (!REF_STATE %in% state_levels) {
  warning("REF_STATE '", REF_STATE, "' not among state levels; ",
          "falling back to '", state_levels[1], "'.")
  REF_STATE <- state_levels[1]
}

if (length(OBS_COVARIATES) > 0)
  warning("Bundled HMM carries observation covariates: ",
          paste(OBS_COVARIATES, collapse = ", "),
          ". This notebook is the covariate-free baseline.")

central_label <- if (CENTRAL_FRAC >= 1)
  "full stayer subpopulation (no central trim)" else
  paste0("deepest ", round(CENTRAL_FRAC * 100), "% of stayers")

cat("Bundle            :", BUNDLE_PATH, "\n")
cat("Patients          :", dplyr::n_distinct(hmm_data$ID), "\n")
cat("Grid days         :", dplyr::n_distinct(hmm_data$time),
    " (0..", max(hmm_data$time), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("Total grid values :", nrow(hmm_data), "\n")
cat("Responses         :", paste(RESPONSE_VARS, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("States            :", N_STATES, " (", paste(state_levels, collapse = ", "),
    ")\n", sep = "")
cat("Reference state   :", REF_STATE, "\n")
cat("Stayer window     : days 0..", STAYER_WINDOW, "\n", sep = "")
cat("Central cut       :", central_label, "\n")
```

## 0.5 Back-transform helpers

```{r helpers}
inv_zscore <- function(z_vals, biomarker_safe) {
  if (!APPLY_ZSCORE) return(z_vals)
  row <- zscore_params[zscore_params$biomarker == biomarker_safe, ]
  z_vals * row$sd + row$mean
}
to_clinical <- function(values, biomarker_safe) {
  v <- inv_zscore(values, biomarker_safe)
  if (isTRUE(needs_expm1[[biomarker_safe]])) v <- expm1(v)
  v
}
axis_label <- function(biomarker_safe) {
  disp <- display(biomarker_safe)
  bits <- character()
  if (isTRUE(needs_expm1[[biomarker_safe]])) bits <- c(bits, "back-transformed from log1p")
  if (APPLY_ZSCORE)                          bits <- c(bits, "model on z-scores")
  if (length(bits) == 0) disp else paste0(disp, " (", paste(bits, collapse = "; "), ")")
}

# Patient-level view of df_full (which is replicated per day).
patient_level <- function(cols) {
  df_full |>
    dplyr::group_by(ID) |>
    dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::any_of(cols),
                                   ~ dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(.x))),
                     .groups = "drop")
}

# Token-exact parse of the pipe-separated admission_reason field.
parse_reasons <- function(s) {
  toks <- unique(trimws(unlist(strsplit(s, "\\|"))))
  toks[toks != ""]
}

# Survival helpers. Defined here rather than inside a gated chunk so that
# every later section can call them.
# NOTE: because these two DO embed the data by value, never print a survfit or
# survdiff object whole — print summary(fit)$table or the components instead,
# or the knitted document will contain the entire data frame.
# survminer inspects fit$call$formula, so the call must embed the formula and
# the data BY VALUE; bquote() does that, reformulate() alone leaves a symbol
# and surv_pvalue() then fails with "object of type 'symbol' is not
# subsettable".
fit_km_one <- function(data, state_col) {
  form <- stats::reformulate(state_col, response = "survival::Surv(time, event)")
  eval(bquote(survival::survfit(.(form), data = .(data))))
}
run_logrank <- function(data, state_col, tag) {
  form <- stats::reformulate(state_col, response = "survival::Surv(time, event)")
  lr <- eval(bquote(survival::survdiff(.(form), data = .(data))))
  p  <- 1 - stats::pchisq(lr$chisq, df = length(lr$n) - 1)
  cat("── Log-rank, ", tag, " ──\n", sep = "")
  print(lr$n)
  cat("chi-squared = ", round(lr$chisq, 3), " (df = ", length(lr$n) - 1,
      "), p = ", format.pval(p, digits = 3, eps = 1e-4), "\n\n", sep = "")
  invisible(tibble::tibble(stratification = tag, chisq = round(lr$chisq, 3),
                           df = length(lr$n) - 1, p = p))
}
```

## 0.6 Outcome integrity checks

Not reported in the thesis. Three consistency checks run before the
outcomes are used as labels: the two binary outcomes must agree, the
three groups encoded by the `days_death_from_discharge` sentinels must
have plausible counts, and the post-discharge time-to-event
distribution must cover a usable range.

```{r outcome-integrity}
po <- patient_level(c(OUTCOME_COLS, DATE_OF_DEATH_COL, ADMISSION_DEATH_COL))
cat("Patients in outcome table: ", nrow(po), "\n\n", sep = "")

if (all(OUTCOME_COLS %in% names(po))) {
  cat("── discharge_dead x discharge_mortality_90d ──\n")
  print(table(discharge_dead          = po$discharge_dead,
              discharge_mortality_90d = po$discharge_mortality_90d,
              useNA = "ifany"))
  # An in-hospital death is a death within 90 days by construction.
  n_anom <- sum(po$discharge_dead == 1 & po$discharge_mortality_90d == 0,
                na.rm = TRUE)
  cat("Logically impossible cells (dead in hospital, not dead at 90d): ",
      n_anom, "\n\n", sep = "")
}

if (DATE_OF_DEATH_COL %in% names(po)) {
  d <- po[[DATE_OF_DEATH_COL]]
  grp <- dplyr::case_when(
    d == -1L ~ "Alive at follow-up (censored)",
    d == -2L ~ "Died in-hospital (excluded from post-discharge KM)",
    d >=  1L ~ "Died post-discharge",
    TRUE     ~ "Other / anomalous")
  cat("── Sentinel breakdown ──\n"); print(table(group = grp, useNA = "ifany"))
  pd <- d[d >= 1L & !is.na(d)]
  if (length(pd) > 0)
    cat("\nPost-discharge deaths: n = ", length(pd),
        "; min/median/max = ", min(pd), " / ", stats::median(pd), " / ",
        max(pd), " days\n", sep = "")
}
```

\newpage

# 1. State-occupancy patterns: stayers and switchers

*Chapter 4, Section 4.1.*

The section that used to open Chapter 3's discussion of occupancy has
been moved here, because Chapter 4 needs the stayer/switcher split as
its first definition: the stayers supply the reference subpopulations
for the depth analysis of Section 2, and the switchers are the
retrospective counterpart of the alert system of Section 6.

## 1.1 Definition and cohort composition

Let $\hat s_{i0},\dots,\hat s_{i,14}$ be the globally decoded sequence
of patient $i$ and $\mathcal S_i$ the set of states it visits. Patient
$i$ is a **stayer** if $|\mathcal S_i| = 1$ and a **switcher**
otherwise. The window is the whole grid.

```{r occupancy-definition}
stopifnot(STAYER_WINDOW == 14L)

patient_states <- hmm_data |>
  dplyr::filter(time <= STAYER_WINDOW) |>
  dplyr::group_by(ID) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_states_visited = dplyr::n_distinct(state),
    sole_state = if (dplyr::n_distinct(state) == 1)
                   as.character(state[1]) else NA_character_,
    pattern    = if (dplyr::n_distinct(state) == 1) "stayer" else "switcher",
    .groups    = "drop")

n_stayer   <- sum(patient_states$pattern == "stayer")
n_switcher <- sum(patient_states$pattern == "switcher")

cat("Stayer / switcher split (window = days 0..", STAYER_WINDOW, "):\n", sep = "")
print(table(patient_states$pattern))
cat("\nNumber of distinct states visited:\n")
print(table(patient_states$n_states_visited))

# Cross-check against Chapter 3. A mismatch means the bundle is not the one
# Chapter 3 was written from.
if (n_stayer != 887L || n_switcher != 152L)
  warning("Stayer/switcher split is ", n_stayer, "/", n_switcher,
          ", not the 887/152 reported in Chapter 3. Verify the bundle.")

tab01 <- patient_states |>
  dplyr::filter(pattern == "stayer") |>
  dplyr::count(sole_state, name = "stayers") |>
  dplyr::mutate(sole_state = factor(sole_state, levels = state_levels)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(sole_state) |>
  dplyr::rename(state = sole_state) |>
  dplyr::mutate(share_of_cohort = round(stayers / nrow(patient_states), 3))

save_tab(tab01, "tab41_01_stayers_by_state",
         caption = paste0("Stayers by state over days 0..", STAYER_WINDOW,
                          ". The remaining ", n_switcher,
                          " patients are switchers."))
```

```{r occupancy-composition-fig, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
p_comp <- tab01 |>
  ggplot(aes(x = state, y = stayers, fill = state)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = stayers), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Stayers by decoded state",
       subtitle = paste0("Window = days 0..", STAYER_WINDOW, ". ",
                         n_stayer, " stayers, ", n_switcher, " switchers, ",
                         nrow(patient_states), " patients."),
       x = NULL, y = "Patients") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
p_comp
save_fig(p_comp, "fig41_01_stayers_by_state", width = 8, height = 4)
```

## 1.2 Decoded state at the three checkpoints

```{r occupancy-alluvial, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
build_alluvial_df <- function(ids, checkpoints) {
  hmm_data |>
    dplyr::filter(ID %in% ids, time %in% checkpoints) |>
    dplyr::select(ID, time, state) |>
    dplyr::mutate(time_lbl = factor(paste0("Day ", time),
                                    levels = paste0("Day ", checkpoints))) |>
    dplyr::select(-time) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time_lbl, values_from = state) |>
    dplyr::count(!!!rlang::syms(paste0("Day ", checkpoints)), name = "Freq")
}

plot_alluvial <- function(df, checkpoints, title, subtitle) {
  axis_args <- setNames(
    lapply(paste0("Day ", checkpoints), function(c) rlang::sym(c)),
    paste0("axis", seq_along(checkpoints)))
  ggplot(df, aes(y = Freq, !!!axis_args)) +
    geom_alluvium(aes(fill = `Day 0`), alpha = 0.7, width = 1/6) +
    geom_stratum(width = 1/6, fill = "grey90", colour = "grey40") +
    geom_text(stat = "stratum", aes(label = after_stat(stratum)), size = 3) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = paste0("Day ", checkpoints),
                     expand = c(0.05, 0.05)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = state_colours, name = "State on admission") +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = NULL, y = "Number of patients") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
}

allu_all <- build_alluvial_df(patient_states$ID, OCCUPANCY_CHECKPOINTS)
p_allu_all <- plot_alluvial(
  allu_all, OCCUPANCY_CHECKPOINTS,
  "Decoded state at admission, one week and end of window",
  paste0("All ", nrow(patient_states),
         " patients. Ribbon width is proportional to the number of patients."))
p_allu_all
save_fig(p_allu_all, "fig41_02_occupancy_alluvial", width = 10, height = 6)
```

## 1.3 When movement occurs

Chapter 3 asserted, from the alluvial diagram alone, that the movement
which does occur concentrates in the first interval. This quantifies
it: the number of patients whose decoded state differs between
consecutive checkpoints, interval by interval.

```{r switch-timing}
cp_states <- hmm_data |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% OCCUPANCY_CHECKPOINTS) |>
  dplyr::select(ID, time, state) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = state,
                     names_prefix = "d")

interval_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(
  seq_len(length(OCCUPANCY_CHECKPOINTS) - 1L), function(k) {
    a <- paste0("d", OCCUPANCY_CHECKPOINTS[k])
    b <- paste0("d", OCCUPANCY_CHECKPOINTS[k + 1L])
    changed <- as.character(cp_states[[a]]) != as.character(cp_states[[b]])
    tibble::tibble(
      interval  = paste0("day ", OCCUPANCY_CHECKPOINTS[k], " \u2192 day ",
                         OCCUPANCY_CHECKPOINTS[k + 1L]),
      n_patients = sum(!is.na(changed)),
      n_changed  = sum(changed, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct        = round(100 * mean(changed, na.rm = TRUE), 2))
  })

save_tab(interval_tbl, "tab41_02_switch_timing",
         caption = paste0("Patients whose globally decoded state differs ",
                          "between consecutive checkpoints."))

# Two-sided test of equality of the two interval proportions (paired on the
# same patients, so McNemar is the correct test).
if (nrow(interval_tbl) == 2) {
  ch1 <- as.character(cp_states$d0) != as.character(cp_states$d7)
  ch2 <- as.character(cp_states$d7) != as.character(cp_states$d14)
  mc  <- stats::mcnemar.test(table(first_interval = ch1, second_interval = ch2))
  cat("\nMcNemar test, early vs late interval:\n"); print(mc)
}
```

```{r switch-timing-fig, fig.width=7, fig.height=4}
p_int <- interval_tbl |>
  ggplot(aes(x = interval, y = n_changed)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#c0392b", width = 0.55, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n_changed, " (", pct, "%)")),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3.4) +
  labs(title = "Where the state changes happen",
       subtitle = "Patients with a different decoded state at the two ends of each interval",
       x = NULL, y = "Patients changing state") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
p_int
save_fig(p_int, "fig41_03_switch_timing", width = 7, height = 4)
```

## 1.4 Emergency-department stabilisation

Chapter 3 offered a clinical reading of the early concentration of
switches: admission to the ward is preceded by a stay in the emergency
department, during which the acute derangement is partly corrected, so
the first ward days record a situation still in motion. That reading is
a hypothesis; here it is confronted with the ED columns, when present.

```{r er-hypothesis, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
er_cols <- intersect(c("days_in_ER", "ER_last_day"), names(df_full))

if (length(er_cols) == 0) {
  cat("No emergency-department column in df_full ",
      "(looked for days_in_ER, ER_last_day). Section skipped.\n", sep = "")
} else {
  er_pt <- patient_level(er_cols) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(patient_states |> dplyr::select(ID, pattern), by = "ID")

  # ER_last_day is a Date, days_in_ER a duration in days. They cannot be
  # stacked into one long column, and only the duration is meaningful on its
  # own: a calendar date is interpretable only relative to the admission date,
  # which is not part of this table. Numeric columns are tested and plotted;
  # anything else is reported and skipped.
  er_num  <- er_cols[vapply(er_pt[er_cols], is.numeric, logical(1))]
  er_skip <- setdiff(er_cols, er_num)

  if (length(er_skip) > 0)
    cat("Non-numeric ED column(s) skipped (",
        paste(er_skip, collapse = ", "), "): a calendar date carries no ",
        "exposure information without the admission date.\n\n", sep = "")

  if (length(er_num) == 0) {
    cat("No numeric ED exposure column available. Section skipped.\n")
  } else {
    er_tests <- purrr::map_dfr(er_num, function(v) {
      x <- er_pt[[v]]; g <- er_pt$pattern
      tibble::tibble(
        variable      = v,
        n_stayer      = sum(g == "stayer"   & !is.na(x)),
        n_switcher    = sum(g == "switcher" & !is.na(x)),
        median_stayer = stats::median(x[g == "stayer"],   na.rm = TRUE),
        median_switch = stats::median(x[g == "switcher"], na.rm = TRUE),
        p_wilcoxon    = tryCatch(
          suppressWarnings(stats::wilcox.test(x ~ g)$p.value),
          error = function(e) NA_real_))
    })
    print(as.data.frame(er_tests), digits = 4, row.names = FALSE)
    save_tab(er_tests, "tab41_03_er_exposure",
             caption = paste0("Emergency-department exposure by occupancy ",
                              "pattern. Tests the stabilisation reading of ",
                              "the early switches."),
             digits = 4)

    p_er <- er_pt |>
      dplyr::select(ID, pattern, dplyr::all_of(er_num)) |>
      tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::all_of(er_num),
                          names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)) |>
      ggplot(aes(x = pattern, y = value, fill = pattern)) +
      geom_boxplot(width = 0.55, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
      facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(stayer = "grey70", switcher = "#c0392b"),
                        guide = "none") +
      labs(title = "Emergency-department exposure by occupancy pattern",
           subtitle = "Tests the stabilisation reading of the early switches",
           x = NULL, y = "Days in the emergency department") +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
    print(p_er)
    save_fig(p_er, "fig41_04_er_exposure", width = 8, height = 4)
  }
}
```
\newpage

# 2. Admission phenotypes from statistical depth

*Chapter 4, Section 4.2.*

The four stayer subpopulations are the best-identified groups the model
produces: a stayer occupies one state for the entire admission, so its
admission vector is an uncontaminated sample from that state's clinical
profile. Each subpopulation is summarised by its **central core**, and
every patient in the cohort — stayers and switchers alike — is then
assigned to the state whose core they are deepest in, using the
admission vector alone.

The assignment uses $\mathbf{Y}^\star_{i0}$ and nothing else. It is
therefore a genuinely baseline-only label, unlike the decoded state at
$t=0$, which under global decoding depends on the patient's whole
subsequent trajectory. Depth is measured with the **Mahalanobis**
depth throughout.

## 2.1 Admission matrices of the stayer subpopulations

```{r stayer-matrices}
day0_stayers <- hmm_data |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    patient_states |>
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(sole_state)) |>
      dplyr::select(ID, sole_state),
    by = "ID") |>
  dplyr::select(ID, sole_state, dplyr::all_of(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE))

cat("Stayers per state (admission sample size for depth):\n")
print(table(factor(day0_stayers$sole_state, levels = state_levels)))

stayer_mats <- split(day0_stayers, factor(day0_stayers$sole_state,
                                          levels = state_levels)) |>
  lapply(function(d) as.matrix(d[, RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE, drop = FALSE]))
```

## 2.2 Central subpopulation and deepest point

Two-step filter. First, drop the formal outliers: a point with
Mahalanobis depth equal to zero lies outside the convex hull of the
subpopulation. Second, if `CENTRAL_FRAC < 1`, retain the deepest
`CENTRAL_FRAC` fraction of what remains.

```{r central-cut}
central_mats <- lapply(stayer_mats, function(M) {
  if (nrow(M) < 5) {
    warning("State with fewer than 5 stayers; depth is unreliable.")
    return(M)
  }
  d <- depth(u = M, X = M, method = "Mahalanobis")
  M_clean <- M[d > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  d_clean <- d[d > 0]
  if (CENTRAL_FRAC < 1) {
    target_n <- ceiling(nrow(M) * CENTRAL_FRAC)
    if (nrow(M_clean) > target_n) {
      ord     <- order(d_clean, decreasing = TRUE)
      M_clean <- M_clean[ord[seq_len(target_n)], , drop = FALSE]
    }
  }
  M_clean
})

tab03 <- tibble::tibble(
  state           = names(stayer_mats),
  n_stayers       = vapply(stayer_mats,  nrow, integer(1)),
  n_central       = vapply(central_mats, nrow, integer(1))) |>
  dplyr::mutate(n_dropped = n_stayers - n_central,
                state = factor(state, levels = state_levels)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(state)

save_tab(tab03, "tab42_01_central_populations",
         caption = paste0("Size of each stayer subpopulation and of its ",
                          "central core (", central_label, ")."))

# Deepest point (Mahalanobis median) of each central population.
state_medians <- lapply(central_mats, function(M)
  depthMedian(M, depth_params = list(method = "Mahalanobis")))
state_medians_df <- do.call(rbind, state_medians) |> as.data.frame()
colnames(state_medians_df) <- RESPONSE_VARS
state_medians_df <- tibble::tibble(state = names(state_medians)) |>
  dplyr::bind_cols(state_medians_df)

state_medians_clin <- state_medians_df
for (i in seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE))
  state_medians_clin[[RESPONSE_VARS[i]]] <-
    to_clinical(state_medians_df[[RESPONSE_VARS[i]]], RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i])

save_tab(state_medians_clin, "tab42_02_deepest_points_clinical",
         caption = paste0("Deepest point of each central population, ",
                          "clinical scale (", central_label, ")."))
save_tab(state_medians_df, "tab42_03_deepest_points_model_scale",
         caption = "Deepest point of each central population, model scale.")
```

## 2.3 Depth distribution per subpopulation

```{r depth-distribution, fig.width=11, fig.height=4}
depth_long <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(stayer_mats), function(s) {
  M <- stayer_mats[[s]]
  data.frame(state = s, depth = depth(u = M, X = M, method = "Mahalanobis"))
}))
depth_long$state <- factor(depth_long$state, levels = state_levels)

thresholds <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(stayer_mats), function(s) {
  d <- depth_long$depth[depth_long$state == s]
  d_pos <- d[d > 0]
  thr <- if (CENTRAL_FRAC < 1) {
    target_n <- ceiling(length(d) * CENTRAL_FRAC)
    if (length(d_pos) > target_n) sort(d_pos, decreasing = TRUE)[target_n]
    else NA_real_
  } else NA_real_
  data.frame(state = factor(s, levels = state_levels), blue_thr = thr)
}))

p_depth <- ggplot(depth_long, aes(x = depth)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red",
             linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ state, ncol = N_STATES, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Mahalanobis depth within each admission subpopulation",
       subtitle = if (CENTRAL_FRAC < 1)
         paste0("Red: depth = 0, outside the convex hull. Blue: the ",
                round(CENTRAL_FRAC * 100), "% central cut.")
       else "Red: depth = 0, outside the convex hull. No central trim.",
       x = "Mahalanobis depth", y = "Patients") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
if (any(!is.na(thresholds$blue_thr)))
  p_depth <- p_depth +
    geom_vline(data = thresholds[!is.na(thresholds$blue_thr), ],
               aes(xintercept = blue_thr), linetype = "dashed",
               colour = "#1a6faf", linewidth = 0.7)
p_depth
save_fig(p_depth, "fig42_02_depth_distributions", width = 11, height = 4)
```

## 2.4 Outlying admission profiles

Patients dropped by the first cut, with their admission biomarkers in
clinical units, so a clinician can judge whether each is a real anomaly
or a benign combination the sample size did not cover.

```{r outlier-inspection}
outlier_inspection <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(stayer_mats), function(s) {
  M <- stayer_mats[[s]]
  d <- depth(u = M, X = M, method = "Mahalanobis")
  out_idx <- which(d <= 0)
  if (length(out_idx) == 0) return(NULL)
  ids <- day0_stayers$ID[day0_stayers$sole_state == s][out_idx]
  M_out  <- M[out_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  M_clin <- vapply(seq_along(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE), function(i)
    to_clinical(M_out[, i], RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE[i]), numeric(length(out_idx)))
  colnames(M_clin) <- RESPONSE_VARS
  data.frame(state = s, patient_id = as.character(ids), round(M_clin, 2),
             check.names = FALSE)
}))

if (is.null(outlier_inspection) || nrow(outlier_inspection) == 0) {
  cat("No depth-0 admission profiles in any subpopulation.\n")
} else {
  save_tab(outlier_inspection, "tab42_04_outlying_admission_profiles",
           caption = paste0("Admission profiles with Mahalanobis depth 0 ",
                            "within their own subpopulation, clinical scale."))
}
```

## 2.5 Depth-based assignment of the whole cohort

Every patient is assigned to the state whose central population their
admission vector is deepest in. Patients whose maximum depth across
states falls below `OUTLIER_DEPTH_THRESHOLD` are flagged as atypical
and still assigned.

```{r classify-all}
classify_one <- function(x_row, central_mats) {
  ds <- vapply(central_mats,
               function(M) depth(u = matrix(x_row, nrow = 1), X = M,
                                 method = "Mahalanobis"),
               numeric(1))
  list(state = names(which.max(ds)), depths = ds,
       is_outlier = max(ds) < OUTLIER_DEPTH_THRESHOLD, max_depth = max(ds))
}

all_day0 <- hmm_data |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 0) |>
  dplyr::select(ID, dplyr::all_of(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE))

cls_all <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(all_day0)), function(k)
  classify_one(as.numeric(all_day0[k, RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE]), central_mats))

all_day0$depth_state <- factor(vapply(cls_all, `[[`, character(1), "state"),
                               levels = state_levels)
all_day0$is_outlier  <- vapply(cls_all, `[[`, logical(1), "is_outlier")
all_day0$max_depth   <- vapply(cls_all, `[[`, numeric(1), "max_depth")

# Depth with respect to every state, kept for the atypicality analysis.
depth_matrix_all <- do.call(rbind, lapply(cls_all, `[[`, "depths"))
colnames(depth_matrix_all) <- names(central_mats)
all_depths <- dplyr::bind_cols(tibble::tibble(ID = all_day0$ID),
                               as.data.frame(depth_matrix_all))

cat("Patients assigned: ", nrow(all_day0), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Flagged atypical (max depth < ", OUTLIER_DEPTH_THRESHOLD, "): ",
    sum(all_day0$is_outlier), "\n", sep = "")

tab06 <- all_day0 |>
  dplyr::count(depth_state, name = "patients") |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = round(patients / nrow(all_day0), 3))
save_tab(tab06, "tab42_05_phenotype_distribution",
         caption = "Distribution of the admission phenotype over the cohort.")
```

```{r atypicality-fig, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
# Depth with respect to EVERY state, not just the winner: the margin between
# the best and the second-best state says how contested the assignment was.
margin_df <- all_depths |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-ID, names_to = "state", values_to = "depth") |>
  dplyr::group_by(ID) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(depth), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::summarise(best = dplyr::first(state),
                   d1 = dplyr::nth(depth, 1), d2 = dplyr::nth(depth, 2),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(margin = d1 - d2,
                best = factor(best, levels = state_levels))

p_margin <- ggplot(margin_df, aes(x = best, y = margin, fill = best)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.alpha = 0.25) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_colours, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Margin between the best and second-best phenotype",
       subtitle = "Small margins mark patients the admission vector does not separate cleanly.",
       x = NULL, y = "Depth margin") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
p_margin
```

# 3. Classification anchors

*Chapter 4, Section 4.3.*

Two anchors are carried forward, and only two. They differ in how much
of the patient's history they are allowed to see.

| Anchor | Information used |
|---|---|
| **admission** | $\mathbf{Y}^\star_{i0}$ alone, via the depth assignment of Section 2 |
| **day-`r DAY_TARGET` online** | $\mathbf{Y}^\star_{i,0:7}$, via Viterbi on the truncated panel |

The day-`r DAY_TARGET` anchor decodes each patient on the panel
restricted to days $0,\dots,$ `r DAY_TARGET` and reads the state at the
final time point. No observation after day `r DAY_TARGET` enters it.
This is leak-free **in time**; it is not, and must never be described
as, out-of-sample: the same patients were used to fit the model.

## 3.1 Online decoding

```{r online-decoder}
# Generalised shadow-HMM online-state builder. Returns one row per patient
# with the leak-free Viterbi state at `target_day`, restricted to patients
# alive at that day and with a complete panel up to it.
# hmmTMB's Viterbi needs at least two time points, so for target_day == 0 we
# decode days 0..1 and read the day-0 state back.
death_from_admission <- if (ADMISSION_DEATH_COL %in% names(df_full)) {
  patient_level(ADMISSION_DEATH_COL) |>
    dplyr::rename(dth_adm = dplyr::all_of(ADMISSION_DEATH_COL))
} else {
  tibble::tibble(ID = unique(hmm_data$ID), dth_adm = NA_integer_)
}

alive_at <- function(day) {
  death_from_admission |>
    dplyr::filter(is.na(dth_adm) | dth_adm == -1L | dth_adm > day) |>
    dplyr::pull(ID)
}

# Trained parameters, rebuilt once and reused by every call.
.obs_par_mat <- hmm$obs()$par(t = 1)[, , 1]
if (IS_a_MVN) {
  .pure <- sub("^z\\.", "", rownames(.obs_par_mat))
  .trained_par <- list(z = setNames(
    lapply(seq_len(nrow(.obs_par_mat)),
           function(i) as.numeric(.obs_par_mat[i, ])), .pure))
  .dists_use <- list(z = "mvnorm")
} else {
  .trained_par <- setNames(lapply(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE, function(b) list(
    mean = as.numeric(.obs_par_mat[paste0(b, ".mean"), ]),
    sd   = as.numeric(.obs_par_mat[paste0(b, ".sd"),   ]))), RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)
  .dists_use <- setNames(rep(list("norm"), length(RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)),
                         RESPONSE_VARS_SAFE)
}
.trained_tpm <- hmm$hid()$tpm(t = 1)
if (length(dim(.trained_tpm)) == 3) .trained_tpm <- .trained_tpm[, , 1]
.trained_tpm <- .trained_tpm / rowSums(.trained_tpm)

build_online_state <- function(target_day) {
  decode_upto <- max(1L, as.integer(target_day))
  ids_alive   <- alive_at(target_day)

  # No column selection: hmmTMB's MVN family needs helper columns created
  # upstream, and a naive select() would drop them.
  panel <- hmm_data |>
    dplyr::filter(time <= decode_upto, ID %in% ids_alive) |>
    dplyr::arrange(ID, time)

  ok <- panel |> dplyr::count(ID) |>
    dplyr::filter(n == decode_upto + 1L) |> dplyr::pull(ID)
  panel <- panel |> dplyr::filter(ID %in% ok)

  if (nrow(panel) == 0)
    return(tibble::tibble(ID = character(), day = integer(),
                          state = factor(character(), levels = state_levels)))

  obs_k <- Observation$new(data = panel, dists = .dists_use,
                           n_states = N_STATES, par = .trained_par)
  hid_k <- MarkovChain$new(data = panel, n_states = N_STATES,
                           tpm = .trained_tpm)
  hmm_k <- HMM$new(obs = obs_k, hid = hid_k, init = hmm)

  panel$state_k <- factor(state_levels[state_remap[hmm_k$viterbi()]],
                          levels = state_levels)
  panel |>
    dplyr::filter(time == target_day) |>
    dplyr::transmute(ID, day = as.integer(target_day), state = state_k)
}
```

```{r day7-online}
  dplyr::transmute(ID, online_state = state)

cat("Patients with a day-", DAY_TARGET, " online state: ",
    nrow(online_day7), " of ", dplyr::n_distinct(hmm_data$ID), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Excluded because dead on or before day ", DAY_TARGET, ": ",

tab08 <- online_day7 |>
```

# 4. In-hospital mortality

*Chapter 4, Section 4.4.*

In-hospital death is a bounded binary outcome and is modelled by logistic
regression. 90-day mortality is a time-to-event outcome and is deferred to
Section 5.

The question is not whether the phenotype predicts death well. It is whether
states estimated from three biomarkers, with no access to outcomes, no
covariates and no supervision, separate patients by mortality at all, and
whether that separation survives adjustment for what the clinician already
knows at the bedside.

## 4.0 Covariate table and adjustment set

```{r covariate-table}
# admission_reason is a pipe-separated field, e.g. "1 | 4 | 10". The match is
# on the exact TOKEN, so "10" and "11" are not read as infection.
base_covars <- intersect(
  c("age", "sex", "Barthel_index", "CIRS_total_score", "Braden_score",
    "ECOG", "length_of_stay_days", "admission_reason"),
  names(df_full))

covariates_pt <- patient_level(c(base_covars, OUTCOME_COLS))

if ("admission_reason" %in% names(covariates_pt)) {
  .ar <- as.character(covariates_pt$admission_reason)
  covariates_pt$admission_infection <- vapply(.ar, function(s)
    if (is.na(s)) NA_integer_ else as.integer(INFECTION_CODE %in% parse_reasons(s)),
    integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  covariates_pt$count_admission_reasons <- vapply(.ar, function(s)
    if (is.na(s)) NA_integer_ else length(parse_reasons(s)),
    integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

# sex as a factor with an explicit reference, so the coefficient name is stable
if ("sex" %in% names(covariates_pt))
  covariates_pt$sex <- factor(as.character(covariates_pt$sex))

ADJUST_USE <- intersect(ADJUST_COVARS, names(covariates_pt))
missing_adj <- setdiff(ADJUST_COVARS, ADJUST_USE)
if (length(missing_adj) > 0)
  warning("Adjustment covariates not found and dropped: ",
          paste(missing_adj, collapse = ", "))

cat("Adjustment set in use: ", paste(ADJUST_USE, collapse = ", "), "\n\n", sep = "")

# Completeness of the adjustment set. Complete-case analysis is only defensible
# if the loss is small; this prints the loss before anything is fitted.
avail <- tibble::tibble(
  covariate = ADJUST_USE,
  n_missing = vapply(ADJUST_USE, function(v) sum(is.na(covariates_pt[[v]])),
                     integer(1)),
  pct_missing = round(100 * vapply(ADJUST_USE, function(v)
    mean(is.na(covariates_pt[[v]])), numeric(1)), 2))
n_complete <- sum(stats::complete.cases(covariates_pt[, ADJUST_USE, drop = FALSE]))
avail <- dplyr::bind_rows(avail, tibble::tibble(
  covariate = "ALL (complete cases)",
  n_missing = nrow(covariates_pt) - n_complete,
  pct_missing = round(100 * (1 - n_complete / nrow(covariates_pt)), 2)))

save_tab(avail, "tab44_01_covariate_availability",
         caption = paste0("Missingness in the adjustment set over the ",
                          nrow(covariates_pt), " patients of the cohort."))

# Descriptive summary of the adjustment set, for the chapter's covariate table.
desc <- purrr::map_dfr(ADJUST_USE, function(v) {
  x <- covariates_pt[[v]]
  if (is.numeric(x) && dplyr::n_distinct(stats::na.omit(x)) > 2)
    tibble::tibble(covariate = v, type = "continuous",
                   summary = sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
                                     stats::median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                                     stats::quantile(x, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
                                     stats::quantile(x, .75, na.rm = TRUE)))
  else
    tibble::tibble(covariate = v, type = "binary / factor",
                   summary = paste(names(table(x)), as.integer(table(x)),
                                   sep = ": ", collapse = "; "))
})
save_tab(desc, "tab44_02_covariate_summary",
         caption = "Adjustment covariates: median [IQR] or counts by level.")
```

```{r collinearity-check, fig.width=6, fig.height=5}
# CIRS and Barthel both index burden of illness and could be collinear, which
# would inflate the standard errors of BOTH and make the adjusted phenotype
# effect look more stable than it is. Checked before use, not after.
num_adj <- ADJUST_USE[vapply(covariates_pt[ADJUST_USE], function(x)
  is.numeric(x) && dplyr::n_distinct(stats::na.omit(x)) > 2, logical(1))]

if (length(num_adj) >= 2) {
  cmat <- stats::cor(covariates_pt[, num_adj, drop = FALSE],
                     use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
  cat("Pairwise correlation among the continuous adjusters:\n")
  print(round(cmat, 3))

  # Variance inflation: each continuous adjuster regressed on the others.
  vif_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(num_adj, function(v) {
    others <- setdiff(num_adj, v)
    if (length(others) == 0) return(NULL)
    r2 <- summary(stats::lm(stats::reformulate(others, response = v),
                            data = covariates_pt))$r.squared
    tibble::tibble(covariate = v, R2_on_others = round(r2, 4),
                   VIF = round(1 / (1 - r2), 3))
  })
  save_tab(vif_tbl, "tab44_03_collinearity",
           caption = "Variance inflation among the continuous adjustment covariates.")

  cl <- as.data.frame(as.table(cmat)); names(cl) <- c("v1", "v2", "r")
  p_cl <- ggplot(cl, aes(v1, v2, fill = r)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1a6faf", mid = "white", high = "#c0392b",
                         midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "r") +
    labs(title = "Correlation among the adjustment covariates",
         x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
  print(p_cl)
  save_fig(p_cl, "fig44_01_covariate_correlation", width = 6, height = 5)
}
```

## 4.1 Model datasets

```{r model-datasets}
as_binary <- function(y) {
  if (is.factor(y))         as.integer(y) - 1L
  else if (is.logical(y))   as.integer(y)
  else if (is.character(y)) as.integer(y %in% c("1", "TRUE"))
  else                      as.integer(y)
}

model_admission <- all_day0 |>
  dplyr::select(ID, state = depth_state, max_depth) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(covariates_pt, by = "ID") |>
  dplyr::mutate(state = stats::relevel(droplevels(state), ref = REF_STATE),
                anchor = "admission")

model_day7 <- online_day7 |>
  dplyr::select(ID, state = online_state) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(covariates_pt, by = "ID") |>
  dplyr::mutate(state = stats::relevel(droplevels(state), ref = REF_STATE),
                anchor = paste0("day", DAY_TARGET, "_online"))

  list(key = "admission",                        data = model_admission),

cat("Day-", DAY_TARGET, " anchor      : ", nrow(model_day7), " patients\n", sep = "")
```

## 4.2 Absolute risk by phenotype

```{r absolute-risk, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
# Wilson score interval: appropriate for proportions near the boundary, unlike
# the Wald interval.
wilson_ci <- function(x, n, conf = 0.95) {
  if (n == 0) return(c(NA, NA))
  z <- stats::qnorm(1 - (1 - conf) / 2)
  p <- x / n; d <- 1 + z^2 / n
  c(lower = (p + z^2 / (2 * n) - z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))) / d,
    upper = (p + z^2 / (2 * n) + z * sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))) / d)
}

risk_tbl <- event_counts |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::mutate(ci = list(wilson_ci(events, n)),
                lower = round(ci[[1]], 4), upper = round(ci[[2]], 4)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(anchor, state, n, events, rate, lower, upper)

save_tab(risk_tbl, "tab44_05_absolute_risk",
         caption = "In-hospital mortality by state and anchor, with 95% Wilson intervals.")

p_risk <- risk_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(state = factor(state, levels = state_levels)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = state, y = rate, fill = state)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.18, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(events, "/", n), y = upper),
            vjust = -0.6, size = 2.9) +
  facet_wrap(~ anchor) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_colours, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))) +
  labs(title = "In-hospital mortality by state",
       subtitle = "95% Wilson intervals. Label = deaths / patients.",
       x = NULL, y = "Observed risk") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
p_risk
save_fig(p_risk, "fig44_02_absolute_risk", width = 9, height = 4.5)
```

## 4.3 Does the phenotype add to bedside information?

The central comparison of this section. $M_0$ contains only what the clinician
has without the model; $M_1$ adds the phenotype. The likelihood-ratio test of
$M_0$ against $M_1$ is the question "is the latent state worth anything on top
of age, sex, function, comorbidity burden and reason for admission".

```{r logistic-nested-helpers}
auc_fn <- function(y, p) {
  y <- as.integer(y); ok <- !is.na(y) & !is.na(p); y <- y[ok]; p <- p[ok]
  n1 <- sum(y == 1); n0 <- sum(y == 0)
  if (n1 == 0 || n0 == 0) return(NA_real_)
  r <- rank(p); (sum(r[y == 1]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0)
}
brier_fn <- function(y, p) mean((p - as.integer(y))^2, na.rm = TRUE)

# Apparent AUC is optimistic because the model was fitted on the same rows.
# Harrell's bootstrap optimism correction quantifies and removes that bias.
optimism_auc <- function(form, data, B = BOOT_B) {
  fit <- stats::glm(form, data = data, family = stats::binomial())
  y   <- data$.y
  app <- auc_fn(y, stats::predict(fit, type = "response"))
  opt <- rep(NA_real_, B)
  for (b in seq_len(B)) {
    idx <- sample.int(nrow(data), nrow(data), replace = TRUE)
    fb <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(
      stats::glm(form, data = data[idx, , drop = FALSE],
                 family = stats::binomial())), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(fb)) next
    a_boot <- auc_fn(y[idx], stats::predict(fb, type = "response"))
    a_orig <- auc_fn(y, stats::predict(fb, newdata = data, type = "response"))
    opt[b] <- a_boot - a_orig
  }
  o <- mean(opt, na.rm = TRUE)
  c(apparent = app, optimism = o, corrected = app - o,
    B_used = sum(!is.na(opt)))
}

# Build the complete-case frame shared by M0 and M1 so the two are nested on
# identical rows; otherwise the LRT is invalid.
build_frame <- function(data, outcome, state_col = "state",
                        adjust = ADJUST_USE) {
  d <- data
  d$.y <- as_binary(d[[outcome]])
  keep <- stats::complete.cases(d[, c(".y", state_col, adjust), drop = FALSE])
  d[keep, , drop = FALSE]
}
```

```{r logistic-nested}
set.seed(BOOT_SEED)

nested_rows <- list(); nested_fits <- list()

for (ad in anchor_defs) {
  d <- build_frame(ad$data, OUTCOME_LOGIT)
  cat("\n=========================================================\n")
  cat("Anchor: ", ad$key, " | outcome: ", OUTCOME_LOGIT,
      " | complete cases: ", nrow(d), " (events ", sum(d$.y), ")\n", sep = "")
  cat("=========================================================\n")

  f_null  <- stats::glm(.y ~ 1, data = d, family = stats::binomial())
  f_state <- stats::glm(stats::reformulate("state", response = ".y"),
                        data = d, family = stats::binomial())
  f_M0    <- stats::glm(stats::reformulate(ADJUST_USE, response = ".y"),
                        data = d, family = stats::binomial())
  f_M1    <- stats::glm(stats::reformulate(c("state", ADJUST_USE), response = ".y"),
                        data = d, family = stats::binomial())

  nested_fits[[ad$key]] <- list(data = d, state = f_state, M0 = f_M0, M1 = f_M1)

  cat("\n--- M0: covariates only ---\n");            print(summary(f_M0))
  cat("\n--- M1: covariates + phenotype ---\n");     print(summary(f_M1))

  lrt <- stats::anova(f_M0, f_M1, test = "LRT")
  cat("\nLikelihood-ratio test, M0 vs M1:\n"); print(lrt)

  # Does the phenotype alone beat the covariates alone? Non-nested, so AIC only.
  for (nm in c("state only", "M0", "M1")) {
    fit <- switch(nm, "state only" = f_state, "M0" = f_M0, "M1" = f_M1)
    oa  <- optimism_auc(stats::formula(fit), d)
    nested_rows[[length(nested_rows) + 1L]] <- tibble::tibble(
      anchor = ad$key, model = nm,
      n = nrow(d), events = sum(d$.y),
      df = length(stats::coef(fit)) - 1,
      AIC = round(stats::AIC(fit), 2), BIC = round(stats::BIC(fit), 2),
      AUC_apparent  = round(oa[["apparent"]], 4),
      AUC_corrected = round(oa[["corrected"]], 4),
      Brier = round(brier_fn(d$.y, stats::predict(fit, type = "response")), 5),
      LRT_vs_M0_df = if (nm == "M1") lrt$Df[2] else NA_integer_,
      LRT_vs_M0_p  = if (nm == "M1") lrt[["Pr(>Chi)"]][2] else NA_real_)
  }
}

nested_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(nested_rows)
save_tab(nested_tbl, "tab44_06_nested_models",
         caption = paste0("Nested logistic models for in-hospital death. ",
                          "AUC_corrected is bootstrap optimism-corrected (B = ",
                          BOOT_B, ")."),
         digits = 5)
```

## 4.4 Odds ratios, crude and adjusted

```{r logistic-or}
plot_forest <- function(td, title, subtitle, xlab = "Odds ratio (log scale)") {
  td <- td |> dplyr::mutate(term = factor(term, levels = rev(unique(term))))
  ggplot(td, aes(x = estimate, y = term)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
    geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high,
                       colour = ifelse(cross_one, "crosses 1", "does not cross 1")),
                   height = 0.2, linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = ifelse(cross_one, "crosses 1", "does not cross 1")),
               size = 2.8) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("crosses 1" = "grey70",
                                   "does not cross 1" = "#1a6faf"), name = NULL) +
    scale_x_log10() +
    facet_grid(model ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, x = xlab, y = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", strip.placement = "outside",
          strip.text.y.left = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 0, hjust = 1),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
}

or_rows <- list()
for (ad in anchor_defs) {
  fits <- nested_fits[[ad$key]]
  for (nm in c("crude", "adjusted")) {
    fit <- if (nm == "crude") fits$state else fits$M1
    td <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
      dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
      dplyr::mutate(term = sub("^state", "", term),
                    anchor = ad$key, model = nm,
                    cross_one = conf.low <= 1 & conf.high >= 1,
                    n = nrow(fits$data), events = sum(fits$data$.y))
    or_rows[[length(or_rows) + 1L]] <- td
  }
}
or_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(or_rows) |>
  dplyr::select(anchor, model, term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value,
                n, events, cross_one)

save_tab(or_table |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                                                 ~ round(.x, 4))),
         "tab44_07_odds_ratios",
         caption = paste0("Odds ratios for in-hospital death. Crude = state ",
                          "only; adjusted = state + ",
                          paste(ADJUST_USE, collapse = ", "),
                          ". Reference state: ", REF_STATE, "."))

# The confounding structure itself is a result: how each odds ratio moves when
# the covariates are added.
shift_tbl <- or_table |>
  dplyr::filter(term %in% state_levels) |>
  dplyr::select(anchor, term, model, estimate) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = estimate) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_change = round(100 * (adjusted - crude) / crude, 1),
                direction = ifelse(adjusted > crude,
                                   "strengthens under adjustment",
                                   "attenuates under adjustment"))
save_tab(shift_tbl, "tab44_08_confounding_shift",
         caption = "Movement of each odds ratio when the adjustment set is added.")
```

## 4.6 Model diagnostics

```{r logistic-diagnostics, fig.width=9, fig.height=4}
# Separation, influence and calibration for the primary model.
prim <- nested_fits[[PRIMARY_ANCHOR]]
fit  <- prim$M1; d <- prim$data

cat("Largest |coefficient| in the primary adjusted model: ",
    round(max(abs(stats::coef(fit)[-1])), 3),
    "  (values above ~10 indicate separation)\n", sep = "")
cat("Largest standard error: ",
    round(max(summary(fit)$coefficients[-1, 2]), 3), "\n\n", sep = "")

infl <- stats::influence.measures(fit)
cat("Observations flagged influential by at least one measure: ",
    sum(apply(infl$is.inf, 1, any)), " of ", nrow(d), "\n", sep = "")
cd_cook <- stats::cooks.distance(fit)
cat("Max Cook's distance: ", round(max(cd_cook, na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n\n", sep = "")

# Calibration by decile of predicted risk.
pr <- stats::predict(fit, type = "response")
dec <- cut(pr, breaks = stats::quantile(pr, seq(0, 1, 0.1)),
           include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
calib <- tibble::tibble(decile = dec, obs = d$.y, pred = pr) |>
  dplyr::group_by(decile) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), predicted = mean(pred),
                   observed = mean(obs), .groups = "drop")
save_tab(calib, "tab44_11_calibration",
         caption = "Calibration of the primary adjusted model by decile of predicted risk.",
         digits = 4)

p_cal <- ggplot(calib, aes(predicted, observed)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, colour = "#1a6faf") +
  geom_line(colour = "#1a6faf", alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(title = "Calibration, in-hospital death",
       subtitle = paste0("Primary adjusted model, ", PRIMARY_ANCHOR,
                         " anchor. Deciles of predicted risk."),
       x = "Predicted risk", y = "Observed risk") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
p_cal
save_fig(p_cal, "fig44_06_calibration", width = 6, height = 5)
```

# 5. 90-day mortality

*Chapter 4, Section 4.5.*

90-day mortality is a time-to-event outcome and is modelled by Cox regression.
The primary analysis is anchored at **admission**, with every death within 90
days treated as an event, in-hospital deaths included. Anchoring at discharge
instead would condition on surviving to discharge, which removes precisely the
patients the phenotype identifies best; that analysis is retained in
Section 5.6 as a secondary one.

## 5.1 Survival datasets

```{r cox-build}
death_adm <- patient_level(ADMISSION_DEATH_COL) |>
  dplyr::rename(days_to_death = dplyr::all_of(ADMISSION_DEATH_COL))

cat("Sentinel breakdown, ", ADMISSION_DEATH_COL, ":\n", sep = "")
print(table(group = dplyr::case_when(
  death_adm$days_to_death == -1L ~ "alive at end of follow-up (censored)",
  death_adm$days_to_death >=  0L ~ "died, day recorded",
  TRUE                           ~ "other / anomalous"), useNA = "ifany"))

build_cox <- function(data, state_col = "state") {
  out <- data |>
    dplyr::inner_join(death_adm, by = "ID") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      .event = as.integer(!is.na(days_to_death) & days_to_death >= 0L &
                          days_to_death <= SURVIVAL_FOLLOWUP),
      # a death recorded on day 0 would give a zero survival time, which coxph
      # drops; half a day keeps the event in the risk set calculation
      .time  = ifelse(.event == 1, pmax(as.numeric(days_to_death), 0.5),
                      as.numeric(SURVIVAL_FOLLOWUP)))
  out[[state_col]] <- stats::relevel(droplevels(out[[state_col]]), ref = REF_STATE)
  out
}

cox_admission <- build_cox(model_admission)
cox_day7      <- build_cox(model_day7)
cox_anchors   <- list(admission = cox_admission,
                      day7      = cox_day7)
names(cox_anchors)[2] <- paste0("day", DAY_TARGET, "_online")

for (nm in names(cox_anchors)) {
  d <- cox_anchors[[nm]]
  cat("\n", nm, ": n = ", nrow(d), ", events = ", sum(d$.event),
      ", median follow-up = ", round(stats::median(d$.time), 1), " days\n", sep = "")
  print(table(state = d[[ "state" ]], event = d$.event))
}
```

## 5.3 Nested Cox models

```{r cox-nested}
cox_frame <- function(d, state_col = "state", adjust = ADJUST_USE) {
  keep <- stats::complete.cases(d[, c(".time", ".event", state_col, adjust),
                                  drop = FALSE])
  d[keep, , drop = FALSE]
}

# IMPORTANT — do NOT wrap this in eval(bquote(...)). bquote() splices the data
# frame into the stored call BY VALUE, so every subsequent print() of the fit
# echoes all 1039 rows and the knitted document runs to hundreds of pages.
# survminer needs that idiom for survfit/survdiff (it re-reads fit$call), but
# coxph does not: passing `d` as a symbol keeps the call one line long. The
# formula is written back into the call so that print() shows the model rather
# than the symbol `form`. x = TRUE stores the design matrix, which is what
# cox.zph() needs, so nothing ever has to re-evaluate the data argument.
cox_fit <- function(d, terms,
                    response = "survival::Surv(.time, .event)") {
  form <- stats::reformulate(terms, response = response)
  fit  <- survival::coxph(form, data = d, x = TRUE)
  fit$call$formula <- form
  fit
}

# Compact report of a Cox fit: model, fit statistics, coefficients, intervals.
# summary.coxph() prints the full call, so fits are reported through this.
print_cox <- function(fit, label = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(label)) cat("--- ", label, " ---\n", sep = "")
  cat("model: ",
      paste(deparse(stats::formula(fit), width.cutoff = 500L), collapse = " "),
      "\n", sep = "")
  s <- summary(fit)
  cat("n = ", fit$n, ", events = ", fit$nevent,
      ", concordance = ", round(unname(s$concordance[1]), 4),
      " (se ", round(unname(s$concordance[2]), 4), ")",
      ", logLik = ", round(as.numeric(stats::logLik(fit)), 3),
      ", AIC = ", round(stats::AIC(fit), 2), "\n", sep = "")
  print(signif(s$coefficients, 4))
  cat("\nexp(coef) with 95% confidence interval:\n")
  print(round(s$conf.int[, c(1, 3, 4), drop = FALSE], 4))
  cat("\n")
  invisible(fit)
}

# anova.coxph names its p-value column "Pr(>|Chi|)"; anova.glm uses "Pr(>Chi)".
# Locating it by pattern is version-proof; indexing by name is not.
anova_p <- function(a) {
  j <- grep("^P", names(a)); if (!length(j)) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(a[[j[1]]][2])
}
anova_df <- function(a) {
  j <- which(names(a) == "Df"); if (!length(j)) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(a[[j[1]]][2])
}
anova_chisq <- function(a) {
  j <- grep("^Chisq$", names(a))
  if (length(j)) return(as.numeric(a[[j[1]]][2]))
  if (!is.null(a$loglik)) return(2 * abs(diff(a$loglik)))
  NA_real_
}

cox_rows <- list(); cox_fits <- list()
for (nm in names(cox_anchors)) {
  d <- cox_frame(cox_anchors[[nm]])
  cat("\n=========================================================\n")
  cat("Cox, anchor: ", nm, " | complete cases: ", nrow(d),
      " (events ", sum(d$.event), ")\n", sep = "")
  cat("=========================================================\n")

  f_state <- cox_fit(d, "state")
  f_M0    <- cox_fit(d, ADJUST_USE)
  f_M1    <- cox_fit(d, c("state", ADJUST_USE))
  cox_fits[[nm]] <- list(data = d, state = f_state, M0 = f_M0, M1 = f_M1)

  print_cox(f_M0, "M0: covariates only")
  print_cox(f_M1, "M1: covariates + phenotype")

  lrt <- stats::anova(f_M0, f_M1)
  cat("Likelihood-ratio test, M0 vs M1: chisq = ",
      round(anova_chisq(lrt), 3), ", df = ", anova_df(lrt), ", p = ",
      format.pval(anova_p(lrt), digits = 4, eps = 1e-12), "\n\n", sep = "")

  for (k in c("state only", "M0", "M1")) {
    fit <- switch(k, "state only" = f_state, "M0" = f_M0, "M1" = f_M1)
    s <- summary(fit)
    cox_rows[[length(cox_rows) + 1L]] <- tibble::tibble(
      anchor = nm, model = k, n = nrow(d), events = sum(d$.event),
      df = length(stats::coef(fit)),
      AIC = round(stats::AIC(fit), 2), BIC = round(stats::BIC(fit), 2),
      concordance = round(unname(s$concordance[1]), 4),
      concordance_se = round(unname(s$concordance[2]), 4),
      loglik = round(as.numeric(stats::logLik(fit)), 3),
      LRT_vs_M0_chisq = if (k == "M1") round(anova_chisq(lrt), 3) else NA_real_,
      LRT_vs_M0_df    = if (k == "M1") anova_df(lrt) else NA_real_,
      LRT_vs_M0_p     = if (k == "M1") anova_p(lrt)  else NA_real_)
  }
}
cox_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(cox_rows)
save_tab(cox_tbl, "tab45_02_nested_cox",
         caption = "Nested Cox models for 90-day mortality from admission.",
         digits = 5)
```

```{r cox-hr, fig.width=9, fig.height=6}
if (nrow(td_adj_cox) > 0) {
  g <- plot_forest(td_adj_cox, "Adjustment covariates, 90-day mortality",
                   "State terms omitted.", xlab = "Hazard ratio (log scale)")
  print(g); save_fig(g, "fig45_03_forest_adjusters", width = 9, height = 5)
}
```

## 5.5

```{r cox-ph-check, fig.width=11, fig.height=7}
zph_rows <- list()
for (nm in names(cox_fits)) {
  z <- survival::cox.zph(cox_fits[[nm]]$M1)
  cat("\n── Schoenfeld residual test, ", nm, " anchor ──\n", sep = "")
  print(z)
  zt <- as.data.frame(z$table); zt$term <- rownames(zt); zt$anchor <- nm
  zph_rows[[length(zph_rows) + 1L]] <- tibble::as_tibble(zt)

  save_base_fig({
    graphics::par(mfrow = c(2, ceiling(nrow(z$table) / 2)))
    plot(z)
    graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  }, paste0("fig45_04_schoenfeld_", nm), width = 11, height = 7)
}
zph_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(zph_rows) |>
  dplyr::select(anchor, term, chisq, df, p)

# Bonferroni across the terms tested within each anchor. Six simultaneous
# tests at the 5% level produce a false flag about one time in four, so the
# raw column alone is not a basis for changing the model.
n_terms <- zph_tbl |> dplyr::filter(term != "GLOBAL") |>
  dplyr::count(anchor, name = "n_tests")
zph_tbl <- zph_tbl |>
  dplyr::left_join(n_terms, by = "anchor") |>
  dplyr::mutate(p_bonferroni = ifelse(term == "GLOBAL", NA_real_,
                                      pmin(1, p * n_tests)))

save_tab(zph_tbl, "tab45_05_proportional_hazards",
         caption = paste0("Schoenfeld residual test of proportional hazards ",
                          "for the adjusted Cox models, with Bonferroni ",
                          "correction across the terms tested within each anchor."),
         digits = 5)

viol <- zph_tbl |> dplyr::filter(p < 0.05, term != "GLOBAL")
state_violates <- "state" %in% viol$term

cat("\n----------------------------------------------------------\n")
if (nrow(viol) == 0) {
  cat("No evidence against proportional hazards at the 5% level.\n")
} else {
  cat("Terms with p < 0.05 (uncorrected):\n"); print(as.data.frame(viol))
  cat("\nDoes the STATE term violate proportional hazards? ",
      if (state_violates) "YES" else "NO", "\n", sep = "")
  if (!state_violates)
    cat("The phenotype effect is therefore constant over the 90-day window:\n",
        "a single hazard ratio describes it, and the violations concern the\n",
        "adjustment covariates only.\n", sep = "")
}
cat("----------------------------------------------------------\n")
```

```{r cox-period-split-helper}
# Two-period counting-process split, done explicitly. survSplit() is avoided
# because it cannot parse a formula whose response variables begin with a dot.
# Subjects are cut at CUT_DAY: those who leave the risk set before it keep a
# single row; the rest contribute an interval on each side of the cut. The
# intervals of one subject do not overlap, so the partial likelihood is
# unchanged and no robust variance is required.
CUT_DAY <- 14

split_two_periods <- function(d, cut = CUT_DAY,
                              time_col = ".time", event_col = ".event") {
  tt <- d[[time_col]]; ev <- d[[event_col]]
  early <- d
  early$tstart <- 0
  early$tstop  <- pmin(tt, cut)
  early$ev     <- ifelse(tt <= cut, ev, 0L)
  early$period <- "early"

  late <- d[tt > cut, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(late) > 0) {
    late$tstart <- cut
    late$tstop  <- late[[time_col]]
    late$ev     <- late[[event_col]]
    late$period <- "late"
  }

  out <- dplyr::bind_rows(early, late)
  out$period <- factor(out$period, levels = c("early", "late"),
                       labels = c(paste0("day 0-", cut),
                                  paste0("day ", cut + 1, "-", SURVIVAL_FOLLOWUP)))
  out <- out[out$tstop > out$tstart, , drop = FALSE]
  out
}

# Period-specific coding of one variable. Outside its own period the variable
# is held at the reference level (factors) or at zero (numeric), so each
# coefficient is interpretable as that period's effect with the other period
# contributing nothing.
make_period_terms <- function(dsplit, var, ref_level = NULL) {
  x <- dsplit[[var]]
  per <- levels(dsplit$period)
  newnames <- character()
  for (k in seq_along(per)) {
    nm <- paste0(var, "__", c("early", "late")[k])
    inper <- dsplit$period == per[k]
    if (is.factor(x) || is.character(x)) {
      xf <- as.character(x)
      base <- if (!is.null(ref_level)) ref_level else levels(factor(xf))[1]
      v <- ifelse(inper, xf, base)
      dsplit[[nm]] <- stats::relevel(factor(v, levels = levels(factor(xf))),
                                     ref = base)
    } else {
      dsplit[[nm]] <- ifelse(inper, as.numeric(x), 0)
    }
    newnames <- c(newnames, nm)
  }
  attr(dsplit, "period_terms") <- newnames
  dsplit
}
```

```{r cox-ph-remedy}
# Two questions are asked, in this order.
#   (A) Are the state hazard ratios robust to relaxing proportionality on the
#       covariates that violate it? This is remediation.
#   (B) Do the state hazard ratios differ between the early and the late
#       period? This is exploratory: the Schoenfeld test did not flag state,
#       so a difference is not expected, but the front-loading reading of
#       Sections 4.1 to 4.3 makes it a question worth answering directly.

d_prim   <- cox_fits[[PRIMARY_ANCHOR]]$data
d_split  <- split_two_periods(d_prim)
cat("Primary anchor: ", nrow(d_prim), " subjects -> ", nrow(d_split),
    " counting-process rows; events preserved: ",
    sum(d_split$ev), " vs ", sum(d_prim$.event), "\n\n", sep = "")
stopifnot(sum(d_split$ev) == sum(d_prim$.event))

viol_vars <- intersect(unique(viol$term[viol$anchor == PRIMARY_ANCHOR]),
                       c("state", ADJUST_USE))
viol_covars <- setdiff(viol_vars, "state")

# ---- (A) relax proportionality on the violating covariates -----------------
if (length(viol_covars) > 0) {
  dA <- d_split; extra <- character()
  for (v in viol_covars) {
    dA <- make_period_terms(dA, v)
    extra <- c(extra, attr(dA, "period_terms"))
  }
  terms_A <- c("state", setdiff(ADJUST_USE, viol_covars), extra)
  fA <- cox_fit(dA, terms_A, response = "survival::Surv(tstart, tstop, ev)")
  cat("=== (A) Proportionality relaxed on: ",
      paste(viol_covars, collapse = ", "), " ===\n", sep = "")
  print_cox(fA)

  # The point of (A): do the state hazard ratios move?
  hr_main <- broom::tidy(cox_fits[[PRIMARY_ANCHOR]]$M1, exponentiate = TRUE,
                         conf.int = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::filter(grepl("^state", term)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(term = sub("^state", "", term), HR_main = estimate,
                     lo_main = conf.low, hi_main = conf.high)
  hr_A <- broom::tidy(fA, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::filter(grepl("^state", term)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(term = sub("^state", "", term), HR_relaxed = estimate,
                     lo_relaxed = conf.low, hi_relaxed = conf.high)
  sens <- dplyr::left_join(hr_main, hr_A, by = "term") |>
    dplyr::mutate(pct_change = round(100 * (HR_relaxed - HR_main) / HR_main, 1))
  cat("\nState hazard ratios, main model vs proportionality-relaxed model:\n")
  print(as.data.frame(sens), digits = 4)
  save_tab(sens |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                                               ~ round(.x, 4))),
           "tab45_06_ph_sensitivity",
           caption = paste0("State hazard ratios before and after relaxing ",
                            "proportional hazards on ",
                            paste(viol_covars, collapse = ", "),
                            ". A small change indicates the phenotype effect ",
                            "is not an artefact of the violation."))
}

# ---- (B) period-specific state effects (exploratory) -----------------------
dB <- make_period_terms(d_split, "state", ref_level = REF_STATE)
state_terms <- attr(dB, "period_terms")
terms_B <- c(state_terms, ADJUST_USE)
fB <- cox_fit(dB, terms_B, response = "survival::Surv(tstart, tstop, ev)")
cat("\n=== (B) Period-specific state effects, cut at day ", CUT_DAY,
    " (exploratory) ===\n", sep = "")
print_cox(fB)

# Formal test that the two periods share one state effect: the period-specific
# model against the main model, which is the constant-effect special case.
f_const <- cox_fit(dB, c("state", ADJUST_USE),
                   response = "survival::Surv(tstart, tstop, ev)")
lrt_B <- stats::anova(f_const, fB)
cat("\nLikelihood-ratio test, constant vs period-specific state effect:\n")
cat("  chisq = ", round(anova_chisq(lrt_B), 3), ", df = ", anova_df(lrt_B),
    ", p = ", format.pval(anova_p(lrt_B), digits = 4, eps = 1e-12),
    "\n\n", sep = "")

ts <- broom::tidy(fB, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("^state__", term)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    period = ifelse(grepl("__early", term),
                    paste0("day 0-", CUT_DAY),
                    paste0("day ", CUT_DAY + 1, "-", SURVIVAL_FOLLOWUP)),
    state  = sub("^state__(early|late)", "", term)) |>
  dplyr::select(period, state, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value)
save_tab(ts |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                                           ~ round(.x, 4))),
         "tab45_07_period_specific_hr",
         caption = paste0("Period-specific state hazard ratios, follow-up ",
                          "split at day ", CUT_DAY,
                          ". Exploratory: the Schoenfeld test did not flag ",
                          "the state term."))
save_tab(tibble::tibble(
    comparison = "constant state effect vs period-specific state effect",
    chisq = round(anova_chisq(lrt_B), 3), df = anova_df(lrt_B),
    p = anova_p(lrt_B)),
  "tab45_08_period_specific_lrt",
  caption = "Likelihood-ratio test for a period-specific state effect.",
  digits = 5)
```

```{r cox-anchor-comparison}
cdx <- build_cox(common_data |> dplyr::rename(state = state_admission),
                 "state") |>
  dplyr::rename(state_admission = state)
cdx$state_day7 <- stats::relevel(droplevels(cdx$state_day7), ref = REF_STATE)
cdx <- cdx[stats::complete.cases(cdx[, c(".time", ".event", "state_admission",
                                         "state_day7", ADJUST_USE),
                                     drop = FALSE]), ]
cat("Common subcohort for the Cox comparison: n = ", nrow(cdx),
    ", events = ", sum(cdx$.event), "\n\n", sep = "")

cox_cmp_fits <- list(
  M0        = cox_fit(cdx, ADJUST_USE),
  admission = cox_fit(cdx, c("state_admission", ADJUST_USE)),
  day7      = cox_fit(cdx, c("state_day7", ADJUST_USE)),

cox_cmp_tbl <- purrr::imap_dfr(cox_cmp_fits, function(fit, nm) {
  s <- summary(fit)
  tibble::tibble(model = nm, n = nrow(cdx), events = sum(cdx$.event),
                 df = length(stats::coef(fit)),
                 AIC = round(stats::AIC(fit), 2),
                 BIC = round(stats::BIC(fit), 2),

                 concordance_se = round(unname(s$concordance[2]), 4))
})

  {a <- stats::anova(cox_cmp_fits$M0, cox_cmp_fits$admission)

                  chisq = round(anova_chisq(a), 3), df = anova_df(a),
                  p = anova_p(a))},
  {a <- stats::anova(cox_cmp_fits$M0, cox_cmp_fits$day7)
   tibble::tibble(comparison = "M0 -> + day-7 state",
                  chisq = round(anova_chisq(a), 3), df = anova_df(a),
                  p = anova_p(a))})
cat("Incremental contribution of each anchor (Cox):\n")
print(as.data.frame(cox_lrt))
save_tab(cox_lrt, "tab45_10_anchor_lrt",
         caption = "Likelihood-ratio tests for the incremental contribution of each anchor, 90-day mortality.",
         digits = 5)
```
