```{r cox-postdischarge, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
# SECONDARY. Time origin = discharge; in-hospital deaths are undefined and
# excluded, which is an informative selection. Reported to show the two
# anchorings agree, not as the primary estimand.
if (DATE_OF_DEATH_COL %in% names(df_full)) {
  death_dis <- patient_level(DATE_OF_DEATH_COL) |>
    dplyr::rename(days_to_death = dplyr::all_of(DATE_OF_DEATH_COL))

  pd <- model_admission |>
    dplyr::inner_join(death_dis, by = "ID") |>
    dplyr::filter(days_to_death != -2L) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      .event = as.integer(days_to_death >= 1L &
                          days_to_death <= SURVIVAL_FOLLOWUP),
      .time  = ifelse(.event == 1, as.numeric(days_to_death),
                      as.numeric(SURVIVAL_FOLLOWUP)))
  pd$state <- stats::relevel(droplevels(pd$state), ref = REF_STATE)
  pd <- pd[stats::complete.cases(pd[, c(".time", ".event", "state", ADJUST_USE),
                                    drop = FALSE]), ]
  cat("Post-discharge (secondary): n = ", nrow(pd), ", events = ",
      sum(pd$.event), "; in-hospital deaths excluded = ",
      sum(death_dis$days_to_death == -2L, na.rm = TRUE), "\n\n", sep = "")

  f_pd <- cox_fit(pd, c("state", ADJUST_USE))
  print_cox(f_pd, "Secondary Cox, time origin = discharge")
  td_pd <- broom::tidy(f_pd, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(term = sub("^state", "", term),
                  n = f_pd$n, events = f_pd$nevent,
                  excluded_inhospital_deaths =
                    sum(death_dis$days_to_death == -2L, na.rm = TRUE))
  save_tab(td_pd |> dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric),
                                                ~ round(.x, 4))),
           "tab45_11_postdischarge_secondary",
           caption = "Secondary Cox model, time origin = discharge, in-hospital deaths excluded.")

  pd$time <- pd$.time; pd$event <- pd$.event
  g_pd <- survminer::ggsurvplot(
    fit_km_one(pd, "state"), data = pd, palette = unname(state_colours),
    conf.int = TRUE, risk.table = TRUE, risk.table.height = 0.26,
    pval = TRUE, pval.method = TRUE, break.time.by = 30,
    xlim = c(0, SURVIVAL_FOLLOWUP),
    xlab = "Days from discharge", ylab = "Post-discharge survival probability",
    legend.title = "admission phenotype", legend.labs = levels(pd$state),
    ggtheme = theme_bw() + theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")),
    title = "Post-discharge survival by admission phenotype (secondary)",
    subtitle = "In-hospital deaths excluded by construction: an informative selection.")
  print(g_pd)
  save_km_fig(g_pd, "fig45_06_km_postdischarge_secondary")
}
```

# 6. Trajectory dynamics and the day-`r DAY_TARGET` alert

*Chapter 4, Section 4.6.*

Section 1 established that roughly one patient in seven changes state
during the admission. Sections 6.1 describes those patients
retrospectively, with the whole trajectory in hand. Sections 6.2 onward
ask the prospective question instead: can a change be detected as it
happens, using only what is known at the time?

That question was not posed for statistical reasons. The ward asked
for model-based support around the end of the first week, which is when
their own clinical review of an ongoing admission takes place. The
alert rule below is the direct translation of that request: at day
`r DAY_TARGET` and every two days thereafter, compare the patient's
current online state with the state at a reference day, and raise a
flag when the two differ.

## 6.1 Switcher trajectories

```{r trajectory-heatmaps, fig.width=10, fig.height=12}
# One row per patient, x = day, fill = decoded state, faceted by outcome.
# Tiles turn light grey from the day of death onwards.
plot_trajectories <- function(outcome_col, is_dead_col = IS_DEAD_COL) {
  if (!outcome_col %in% names(df_full)) return(NULL)
  if (!is_dead_col %in% names(df_full)) return(NULL)

  pid_outcome <- df_full |>
    dplyr::group_by(ID) |>
    dplyr::summarise(outcome = dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(.data[[outcome_col]])),
                     .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(outcome))

  is_dead_long <- df_full |>
    dplyr::select(ID, time, dplyr::all_of(is_dead_col)) |>
    dplyr::rename(is_dead = !!is_dead_col)

  dstate <- hmm_data |>
    dplyr::left_join(is_dead_long, by = c("ID", "time")) |>
    dplyr::mutate(state_or_dead = dplyr::if_else(
      !is.na(is_dead) & is_dead == 1, NA_character_, as.character(state)))

  pid_order <- dstate |>
    dplyr::inner_join(pid_outcome, by = "ID") |>
    dplyr::arrange(ID, time) |>
    dplyr::group_by(ID) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      outcome     = dplyr::first(outcome),
      first_state = match(state_or_dead[which.min(time)], state_levels),
      worst_state = suppressWarnings(max(match(state_or_dead, state_levels),
                                         na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(worst_state = ifelse(is.infinite(worst_state), NA_integer_,
                                       worst_state)) |>
    dplyr::arrange(outcome, first_state, worst_state) |>
    dplyr::group_by(outcome) |>
    dplyr::mutate(rank_in_facet = dplyr::row_number()) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  plot_df <- dstate |>
    dplyr::inner_join(pid_order, by = "ID") |>
    dplyr::mutate(state_factor = factor(state_or_dead, levels = state_levels),
                  outcome_lbl  = paste0(outcome_col, " = ", outcome))

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = time, y = rank_in_facet, fill = state_factor)) +
    geom_tile(width = 1, height = 1) +
    facet_grid(outcome_lbl ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y",
               switch = "y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = state_colours, na.value = "grey85",
                      name = "State", na.translate = TRUE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 14, 2), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_reverse(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(title = paste0("Decoded trajectories by ", outcome_col),
         subtitle = "Light grey: patient deceased on or after that day. Sorted by first, then worst state.",
         x = "Day", y = "Patient (ranked)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    theme(strip.placement = "outside",
          strip.text.y.left = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 0, hjust = 1),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
}

for (oc in TRAJECTORY_OUTCOMES) {
  g <- plot_trajectories(oc)
  if (is.null(g)) { cat("Trajectory heatmap skipped for ", oc, ".\n", sep = ""); next }
  print(g)
  save_fig(g, paste0("fig46_03_trajectories_", oc), width = 10, height = 12)
}
```

## 6.2 The alert rule

At each check day the patient's online state is compared with the state
at a reference day. The first check is at day `r DAY_TARGET` and is
compared against admission, so it summarises the whole first week; the
later checks are compared against the state two days earlier, so they
detect fresh movement rather than re-reporting an old change. Every
state used here is an online state: at check day $d$ the model has seen
days $0,\dots,d$ and nothing else.

```{r alert-config}
ALERT_PAIRS <- tibble::tibble(check_day = ALERT_CHECK_DAYS,
                              prev_day  = ALERT_PREV_DAYS)
alert_days_all <- sort(unique(c(ALERT_PAIRS$check_day, ALERT_PAIRS$prev_day)))

cat("Online states required at days: ",
    paste(alert_days_all, collapse = ", "), "\n", sep = "")
print(ALERT_PAIRS)
```

```{r alert-online-states}
online_states <- purrr::map_dfr(alert_days_all, build_online_state)

cat("\nOnline-state rows built: ", nrow(online_states), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Patients per checkpoint:\n")
print(online_states |> dplyr::count(day))
```

```{r alert-detection}
alerts <- purrr::pmap_dfr(ALERT_PAIRS, function(check_day, prev_day) {
  now  <- online_states |> dplyr::filter(day == check_day) |>
            dplyr::transmute(ID, state_now = state)
  prev <- online_states |> dplyr::filter(day == prev_day) |>
            dplyr::transmute(ID, state_prev = state)
  dplyr::inner_join(now, prev, by = "ID") |>
    dplyr::mutate(check_day = check_day, prev_day = prev_day,
                  alert = state_now != state_prev)
})

patient_alert <- alerts |>
  dplyr::group_by(ID) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_alerts    = sum(alert),
                   ever_alert  = any(alert),
                   first_alert_day = if (any(alert)) min(check_day[alert])
                                     else NA_integer_,
                   .groups = "drop")

cat("Patients evaluated: ", dplyr::n_distinct(alerts$ID), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Patients with at least one alert: ", sum(patient_alert$ever_alert),
    " (", round(100 * mean(patient_alert$ever_alert), 1), "%)\n\n", sep = "")

window_tbl <- alerts |>
  dplyr::group_by(check_day, prev_day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n_evaluated = dplyr::n(), n_alerts = sum(alert),
                   pct = round(100 * mean(alert), 2), .groups = "drop")
save_tab(window_tbl, "tab46_02_alerts_per_window",
         caption = "Alerts raised at each checkpoint, with the reference day used for the comparison.")
```

```{r alert-heatmaps, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=4.8}
changes_grid <- function(sub, panel) {
  tab <- sub |>
    dplyr::count(state_prev, state_now, name = "n") |>
    tidyr::complete(state_prev = state_levels, state_now = state_levels,
                    fill = list(n = 0))
  tab$n[as.character(tab$state_prev) == as.character(tab$state_now)] <- NA
  tab$panel      <- panel
  tab$state_prev <- factor(tab$state_prev, levels = state_levels)
  tab$state_now  <- factor(tab$state_now,  levels = rev(state_levels))
  tab
}

heat_layer <- function(df) {
  ggplot(df, aes(state_prev, state_now, fill = n)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(n) | n == 0, "", n)), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#fde0d9", high = "#c0392b", na.value = "grey96",
                        name = "Patients") +
    labs(x = "State (from)", y = "State (to)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1),
          panel.grid = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8))
}

p_heat_tot <- heat_layer(changes_grid(alerts, "Total")) +

       subtitle = "All checkpoint windows pooled; the diagonal is blanked.")
p_heat_tot
save_fig(p_heat_tot, "fig46_05_alert_changes_total", width = 5.5, height = 4.8)
```

## 6.4 The alerted population against the Chapter 3 switchers

The two populations are not the same object and must not be conflated.
A **switcher** is defined retrospectively, from the globally decoded
sequence over the whole admission. An **alerted patient** is defined
prospectively, from online states at four fixed checkpoints, and only
for patients still alive and panelled at those days. The cross-tabulation
below quantifies how much of the retrospective picture the prospective
rule recovers.

```{r alert-vs-switcher}
cmp_pop <- patient_alert |>
  dplyr::inner_join(patient_states |> dplyr::select(ID, pattern), by = "ID")

tab_pop <- table(occupancy = cmp_pop$pattern,
                 alerted   = cmp_pop$ever_alert)
cat("Chapter-3 occupancy pattern x alert status (n = ", nrow(cmp_pop), "):\n",
    sep = "")
print(tab_pop)
cat("\nRow proportions:\n"); print(round(prop.table(tab_pop, margin = 1), 3))

sens <- tab_pop["switcher", "TRUE"] / sum(tab_pop["switcher", ])
spec <- tab_pop["stayer",  "FALSE"] / sum(tab_pop["stayer", ])
cat("\nShare of switchers that raise at least one alert: ",
    round(100 * sens, 1), "%\n", sep = "")
cat("Share of stayers that never alert: ", round(100 * spec, 1), "%\n", sep = "")

pop_df <- as.data.frame(tab_pop); names(pop_df) <- c("occupancy", "alerted", "n")
save_tab(pop_df, "tab46_03_alert_vs_switcher",
         caption = "Retrospective occupancy pattern against prospective alert status.")
```

```{r alert-vs-switcher-fig, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4}
  geom_bar(position = "fill", width = 0.6) +

                    name = "Ever alerted") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Alert status within each occupancy pattern",
       subtitle = "Retrospective definition on the x-axis, prospective rule in the fill.",
       x = NULL, y = "Share of patients") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
p_pop
save_fig(p_pop, "fig46_09_alert_vs_switcher", width = 6.5, height = 4)
```

## 6.5 Who raises an alert?

Patients who alert are compared with those who do not on the admission
covariates. Continuous covariates use the Wilcoxon rank-sum test,
categorical ones Fisher's exact test when any expected count falls
below five and the chi-square test otherwise. Because the comparison
spans a long covariate list, p-values are reported both raw and
adjusted by the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure; the adjusted column is
the one to read.

```{r alert-covariates}
covars_pt <- df_full |>
  dplyr::group_by(ID) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(
    dplyr::any_of(c(STRAT_CONTINUOUS, STRAT_CATEGORICAL, "admission_reason")),
    ~ dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(.x))), .groups = "drop")

strat <- dplyr::inner_join(patient_alert, covars_pt, by = "ID")

# Admission-reason features. Codes are pipe-separated, e.g. "1 | 4 | 10", and
# the match is on the exact TOKEN, so "10" and "11" are not read as infection.
if ("admission_reason" %in% names(strat)) {
  .ar <- as.character(strat$admission_reason)
  strat$admission_infection <- vapply(.ar, function(s)
    if (is.na(s)) NA_integer_
    else as.integer(INFECTION_CODE %in% parse_reasons(s)),
    integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  strat$count_admission_reasons <- vapply(.ar, function(s)
    if (is.na(s)) NA_integer_ else length(parse_reasons(s)),
    integer(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  cat("Admission reason parsed. Patients admitted with an infection code (",
      INFECTION_CODE, "): ", sum(strat$admission_infection == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
      " of ", sum(!is.na(strat$admission_infection)), "\n", sep = "")
}

# Carry the two anchors into the stratification table as well.
strat <- strat |>
  dplyr::left_join(all_day0 |> dplyr::select(ID, depth_state), by = "ID") |>
  dplyr::left_join(online_day7, by = "ID")

cat("Stratification cohort: ", nrow(strat), " patients (",
    sum(strat$ever_alert), " with at least one alert).\n\n", sep = "")
```

```{r alert-stratification-tests}
cont_present <- intersect(STRAT_CONTINUOUS, names(strat))
cont_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(cont_present, function(v) {
  x <- strat[[v]]; g <- strat$ever_alert
  if (!is.numeric(x) || dplyr::n_distinct(g) < 2)
    return(tibble::tibble(covariate = v, type = "continuous",
                          summary_alert = NA_character_,
                          summary_noalert = NA_character_, p = NA_real_))
  fmt <- function(z) sprintf("%.1f [%.1f, %.1f]",
                             stats::median(z, na.rm = TRUE),
                             stats::quantile(z, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
                             stats::quantile(z, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE))
  tibble::tibble(
    covariate = v, type = "continuous",
    summary_alert   = fmt(x[g]),
    summary_noalert = fmt(x[!g]),
    p = tryCatch(suppressWarnings(stats::wilcox.test(x ~ g)$p.value),
                 error = function(e) NA_real_))
})

cat_present <- setdiff(intersect(STRAT_CATEGORICAL, names(strat)),
                       "admission_reason")
cat_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(cat_present, function(v) {
  tab <- table(strat[[v]], strat$ever_alert)
  if (nrow(tab) < 2 || ncol(tab) < 2)
    return(tibble::tibble(covariate = v, type = "categorical",
                          summary_alert = NA_character_,
                          summary_noalert = NA_character_, p = NA_real_))
  use_fisher <- any(suppressWarnings(stats::chisq.test(tab)$expected) < 5)
  p <- tryCatch(
    if (use_fisher) stats::fisher.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 5000)$p.value
    else suppressWarnings(stats::chisq.test(tab)$p.value),
    error = function(e) NA_real_)
  tibble::tibble(covariate = v,
                 type = paste0("categorical (",
                               if (use_fisher) "Fisher" else "chi-square", ")"),
                 summary_alert = NA_character_, summary_noalert = NA_character_,
                 p = p)
})

strat_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(cont_tbl, cat_tbl) |>
  dplyr::mutate(p_adj = stats::p.adjust(p, method = P_ADJUST_METHOD)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(p_adj)

save_tab(strat_tbl |>
           dplyr::mutate(p = signif(p, 4), p_adj = signif(p_adj, 4)),
         "tab46_04_alert_stratification",
         caption = paste0("Admission covariates by alert status. p_adj is the ",
                          P_ADJUST_METHOD,
                          "-adjusted p-value across the ", nrow(cont_tbl) + nrow(cat_tbl),
                          " tests in this table and is the one to read."))

# Level-by-level proportions for the categorical covariates.
prop_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(cat_present, function(v) {
  x <- as.character(strat[[v]]); g <- strat$ever_alert
  keep <- !is.na(x); x <- x[keep]; g <- g[keep]
  purrr::map_dfr(sort(unique(x)), function(l) tibble::tibble(
    variable = v, level = l, n = sum(x == l),
    pct_total    = round(100 * mean(x == l), 1),
    pct_no_alert = round(100 * mean(x[!g] == l), 1),
    pct_alert    = round(100 * mean(x[g]  == l), 1)))
})
save_tab(prop_tbl, "tab46_05_alert_categorical_levels",
         caption = "Composition of the categorical covariates by alert status.")
```

## 6.6 Prognostic content of the alert

Three questions, in order: does alerting carry information about the
outcome; how would the rule behave as a ward instrument; and is the
association anything more than the base rate.

```{r alert-logistic}
alert_predictors <- c("ever_alert", intersect(ADJUST_COVARS, names(strat)))

alert_or_rows <- list()
for (oc in intersect(OUTCOME_COLS, names(strat))) {
  for (spec in list(list(lbl = "crude",    pr = "ever_alert"),
                    list(lbl = "adjusted", pr = alert_predictors))) {
    d <- strat |> dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(oc, spec$pr))) |> tidyr::drop_na()
    d[[oc]] <- as_binary(d[[oc]])
    if (dplyr::n_distinct(d[[oc]]) < 2) next
    fit <- stats::glm(stats::reformulate(spec$pr, response = oc),
                      data = d, family = stats::binomial())
    r2 <- 1 - fit$deviance / fit$null.deviance
    cat("── ", oc, " ~ ", paste(spec$pr, collapse = " + "),
        "  (n = ", nrow(d), ", McFadden pseudo-R2 = ", round(r2, 4), ")\n",
        sep = "")
    tt <- broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
      dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
      dplyr::mutate(outcome = oc, model = spec$lbl, n = nrow(d),
                    cross_one = conf.low <= 1 & conf.high >= 1)
    print(as.data.frame(tt |> dplyr::select(term, estimate, conf.low,
                                            conf.high, p.value)), digits = 4)
    cat("\n")
    alert_or_rows[[length(alert_or_rows) + 1L]] <- tt
  }
}
alert_or <- dplyr::bind_rows(alert_or_rows)
save_tab(alert_or |> dplyr::select(outcome, model, term, estimate, conf.low,
                                   conf.high, p.value, n) |>
           dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))),
         "tab46_07_alert_odds_ratios",
         caption = paste0("Odds ratios for the alert, crude and adjusted for ",
                          paste(ADJUST_COVARS, collapse = ", "), "."))
```

```{r alert-operating-characteristics}
# The rule read as a ward instrument. "Reviews per event" is the number of
# alerted patients a clinician would look at for each alerted patient who
# subsequently experiences the outcome.
op_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(intersect(OUTCOME_COLS, names(strat)), function(oc) {
  d <- strat |> dplyr::select(ever_alert, dplyr::all_of(oc)) |> tidyr::drop_na()
  y <- as_binary(d[[oc]]); a <- d$ever_alert
  tp <- sum(a & y == 1); fp <- sum(a & y == 0)
  fn <- sum(!a & y == 1); tn <- sum(!a & y == 0)
  tibble::tibble(
    outcome = oc, n = nrow(d), events = sum(y == 1),
    alerted = sum(a),
    sensitivity = round(tp / (tp + fn), 3),
    specificity = round(tn / (tn + fp), 3),
    PPV = round(tp / (tp + fp), 3),
    NPV = round(tn / (tn + fn), 3),
    reviews_per_event = ifelse(tp == 0, NA_real_, round((tp + fp) / tp, 2)))
})
save_tab(op_tbl, "tab46_08_operating_characteristics",
         caption = "The alert rule read as a screening instrument for each outcome.")
```

```{r alert-lead-time, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
# How much warning the alert gives: days between the first alert and death or
# discharge.
lead_cols <- intersect(c(ADMISSION_DEATH_COL, "length_of_stay_days"),
                       names(df_full))
if (length(lead_cols) > 0) {
  lead <- patient_alert |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(first_alert_day)) |>
    dplyr::left_join(patient_level(lead_cols), by = "ID")
  if (ADMISSION_DEATH_COL %in% names(lead))
    lead$days_to_death_after_alert <- ifelse(
      !is.na(lead[[ADMISSION_DEATH_COL]]) & lead[[ADMISSION_DEATH_COL]] >= 0,
      lead[[ADMISSION_DEATH_COL]] - lead$first_alert_day, NA_real_)
  if ("length_of_stay_days" %in% names(lead))
    lead$days_to_discharge_after_alert <-
      lead$length_of_stay_days - lead$first_alert_day

  lead_long <- lead |>
    dplyr::select(ID, dplyr::any_of(c("days_to_death_after_alert",
                                      "days_to_discharge_after_alert"))) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-ID, names_to = "horizon", values_to = "days") |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(days))

  if (nrow(lead_long) > 0) {
    lead_summary <- lead_long |>
      dplyr::group_by(horizon) |>
      dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(),
                       median = stats::median(days),
                       q25 = stats::quantile(days, 0.25),
                       q75 = stats::quantile(days, 0.75), .groups = "drop")
    save_tab(lead_summary, "tab46_09_lead_time",
             caption = "Days between the first alert and death or discharge.")

    p_lead <- ggplot(lead_long, aes(x = days, fill = horizon)) +
      geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, colour = "white", alpha = 0.9) +
      facet_wrap(~ horizon, scales = "free") +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(days_to_death_after_alert = "#c0392b",
                                   days_to_discharge_after_alert = "#1a6faf"),
                        guide = "none") +
      labs(title = "Warning given by the alert",
           subtitle = "Days from the first alert to the event.",
           x = "Days", y = "Patients") +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
    print(p_lead)
    save_fig(p_lead, "fig46_14_lead_time", width = 8, height = 4)
  }
}
```

```{r alert-permutation, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
# Negative control. The alert labels are permuted PERM_B times, holding the
# marginal alert rate fixed, and the observed association is compared against
# the resulting null distribution. This separates signal from base rate.
set.seed(PERM_SEED)

perm_rows <- list(); perm_draws <- list()
for (oc in intersect(OUTCOME_COLS, names(strat))) {
  d <- strat |> dplyr::select(ever_alert, dplyr::all_of(oc)) |> tidyr::drop_na()
  y <- as_binary(d[[oc]]); a <- as.integer(d$ever_alert)
  if (dplyr::n_distinct(y) < 2) next
  stat_fn <- function(av) mean(y[av == 1]) - mean(y[av == 0])
  obs <- stat_fn(a)
  null_draws <- replicate(PERM_B, stat_fn(sample(a)))
  p_perm <- (1 + sum(abs(null_draws) >= abs(obs))) / (PERM_B + 1)
  perm_rows[[length(perm_rows) + 1L]] <- tibble::tibble(
    outcome = oc, observed_risk_difference = round(obs, 4),
    null_mean = round(mean(null_draws), 4),
    null_sd = round(stats::sd(null_draws), 4),
    p_permutation = signif(p_perm, 4), B = PERM_B)
  perm_draws[[oc]] <- tibble::tibble(outcome = oc, stat = null_draws,
                                     observed = obs)
}
perm_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(perm_rows)
if (nrow(perm_tbl) > 0)
  save_tab(perm_tbl, "tab46_10_permutation",
           caption = paste0("Permutation negative control: the alert labels are ",
                            "reshuffled ", PERM_B, " times at a fixed marginal rate."))

if (length(perm_draws) > 0) {
  pd <- dplyr::bind_rows(perm_draws)
  p_perm_fig <- ggplot(pd, aes(x = stat)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40, fill = "grey75", colour = "white") +
    geom_vline(aes(xintercept = observed), colour = "#c0392b", linewidth = 0.9) +
    facet_wrap(~ outcome, scales = "free") +
    labs(title = "Permutation null for the alert",
         subtitle = "Red line: observed difference in risk between alerted and non-alerted patients.",
         x = "Risk difference under permuted labels", y = "Draws") +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9))
  print(p_perm_fig)
  save_fig(p_perm_fig, "fig46_15_permutation_null", width = 8, height = 4)
}
```

## 6.6bis 

```{r alert-destination}
# Whether a patient moves and where they move to are different questions. The
# alert flags the first; this examines the second. For each alerted patient the
# destination is the online state recorded at their FIRST alert, so the
# quantity is available at the moment the alert fires.
dest <- alerts |>
  dplyr::filter(alert) |>
  dplyr::group_by(ID) |>
  dplyr::slice_min(check_day, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::transmute(ID, first_alert_day = check_day,
                   origin = state_prev, destination = state_now)

alert_dest <- patient_alert |>
  dplyr::select(ID, ever_alert) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dest |> dplyr::select(ID, origin, destination), by = "ID") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Three-level exposure on the whole evaluated cohort: no alert, an alert
    # into the reference state, an alert into any other state.
    alert_type = dplyr::case_when(
      !ever_alert                              ~ "no alert",
      as.character(destination) == REF_STATE   ~ paste0("alert into ", REF_STATE),
      TRUE                                     ~ "alert into another state"),
    alert_type = factor(alert_type,
      levels = c("no alert", paste0("alert into ", REF_STATE),
                 "alert into another state"))) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(covariates_pt, by = "ID")

cat("Exposure groups:\n"); print(table(alert_dest$alert_type))
cat("\nOrigin -> destination at the first alert:\n")
print(table(origin = dest$origin, destination = dest$destination))

# Mortality by destination among the alerted only.
dest_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(intersect(OUTCOME_COLS, names(alert_dest)), function(oc) {
  alert_dest |>
    dplyr::filter(ever_alert, !is.na(destination)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(.y = as_binary(.data[[oc]])) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.y)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(destination) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), events = sum(.y),
                     rate = round(mean(.y), 4), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(outcome = oc)
}) |> dplyr::select(outcome, destination, n, events, rate)

save_tab(dest_tbl, "tab46_14_mortality_by_alert_destination",
         caption = "Mortality among alerted patients, by the state they moved into at the first alert.")

# Three-level exposure, adjusted, on the whole evaluated cohort.
dest_or <- purrr::map_dfr(intersect(OUTCOME_COLS, names(alert_dest)), function(oc) {
  d <- alert_dest |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(oc, "alert_type", ADJUST_USE))) |>
    tidyr::drop_na()
  d[[oc]] <- as_binary(d[[oc]])
  if (dplyr::n_distinct(d[[oc]]) < 2) return(NULL)
  fit <- stats::glm(stats::reformulate(c("alert_type", ADJUST_USE),
                                       response = oc),
                    data = d, family = stats::binomial())
  f0 <- stats::glm(stats::reformulate(ADJUST_USE, response = oc),
                   data = d, family = stats::binomial())
  a <- stats::anova(f0, fit, test = "LRT")
  cat("\n--- ", oc, " ~ alert_type + covariates (n = ", nrow(d), ") ---\n", sep = "")
  cat("LRT against covariates only: deviance = ", round(a$Deviance[2], 3),
      ", df = ", a$Df[2], ", p = ",
      format.pval(a[["Pr(>Chi)"]][2], digits = 4, eps = 1e-12), "\n", sep = "")
  broom::tidy(fit, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::filter(grepl("alert_type", term)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(term = sub("^alert_type", "", term), outcome = oc,
                  n = nrow(d), lrt_p = a[["Pr(>Chi)"]][2],
                  cross_one = conf.low <= 1 & conf.high >= 1)
})
if (!is.null(dest_or) && nrow(dest_or) > 0)
  save_tab(dest_or |> dplyr::select(outcome, term, estimate, conf.low,
                                    conf.high, p.value, lrt_p, n) |>
             dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4))),
           "tab46_15_alert_destination_odds_ratios",
           caption = paste0("Odds ratios for the three-level alert exposure, ",
                            "reference = no alert, adjusted for ",
                            paste(ADJUST_USE, collapse = ", "), "."))
```

## 6.7 Stratification of the alerted patients: admission with infection

The clinical question behind the alert is not only who moves, but which
of the patients who move are at the greatest risk. The stratifying
variable is whether the admission was coded with the infection reason
(token `r INFECTION_CODE` of the pipe-separated `admission_reason`
field). Note that no inflammatory marker enters the model: CRP is not
part of the response set, so "admitted with an infection" is a
documented reason for admission, not a biomarker-derived state.

```{r infection-stratification}
if (!"admission_infection" %in% names(strat)) {
  cat("admission_reason not available; Section 6.7 skipped.\n")
} else {
  inf <- strat |> dplyr::filter(!is.na(admission_infection)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(infection = factor(admission_infection, levels = c(0, 1),
                                     labels = c("no infection code",
                                                "infection code")),
                  group = interaction(ever_alert, infection, sep = " / "))

  cat("Alert x infection (n = ", nrow(inf), "):\n", sep = "")
  tab_inf <- table(alerted = inf$ever_alert, infection = inf$infection)
  print(tab_inf)
  print(stats::fisher.test(tab_inf))

  # Outcome by the four cells.
  cell_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(intersect(OUTCOME_COLS, names(inf)), function(oc) {
    inf |>
      dplyr::mutate(.y = as_binary(.data[[oc]])) |>
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(.y)) |>
      dplyr::group_by(alerted = ever_alert, infection) |>
      dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n(), events = sum(.y),
                       rate = round(mean(.y), 3), .groups = "drop") |>
      dplyr::mutate(outcome = oc)
  }) |>
    dplyr::select(outcome, alerted, infection, n, events, rate)

  save_tab(cell_tbl, "tab46_11_infection_cells",
           caption = paste0("Outcome rate in the four cells defined by alert ",
                            "status and admission with an infection code."))
}
```

```{r infection-interaction}
if ("admission_infection" %in% names(strat)) {
  int_rows <- list()
  for (oc in intersect(OUTCOME_COLS, names(strat))) {
    d <- strat |>
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(c(oc, "ever_alert", "admission_infection",
                                    intersect(ADJUST_COVARS, names(strat))))) |>
      tidyr::drop_na()
    d[[oc]] <- as_binary(d[[oc]])
    if (dplyr::n_distinct(d[[oc]]) < 2) next

    base_terms <- c("ever_alert * admission_infection",
                    intersect(ADJUST_COVARS, names(d)))
    fit_int  <- stats::glm(stats::reformulate(base_terms, response = oc),
                           data = d, family = stats::binomial())
    fit_main <- stats::glm(stats::reformulate(
      c("ever_alert", "admission_infection", intersect(ADJUST_COVARS, names(d))),
      response = oc), data = d, family = stats::binomial())
    lrt <- stats::anova(fit_main, fit_int, test = "LRT")

    cat("── ", oc, ": alert x infection interaction (n = ", nrow(d), ") ──\n",
        sep = "")
    print(as.data.frame(
      broom::tidy(fit_int, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
        dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
        dplyr::select(term, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value)),
      digits = 4)
    cat("Likelihood-ratio test for the interaction: deviance = ",
        round(lrt$Deviance[2], 3), ", df = ", lrt$Df[2], ", p = ",
        format.pval(lrt[["Pr(>Chi)"]][2], digits = 3, eps = 1e-4), "\n\n",
        sep = "")

    int_rows[[length(int_rows) + 1L]] <- tibble::tibble(
      outcome = oc, n = nrow(d),
      lrt_deviance = round(lrt$Deviance[2], 3), lrt_df = lrt$Df[2],
      lrt_p = lrt[["Pr(>Chi)"]][2])
  }
  if (length(int_rows) > 0)
    save_tab(dplyr::bind_rows(int_rows), "tab46_12_infection_interaction",
             caption = "Likelihood-ratio test for the interaction between alerting and admission with an infection code.",
             digits = 5)
}
```

```{r admission-reason-cooccurrence, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
# Context for the infection code: how the eleven admission reasons combine.
if ("admission_reason" %in% names(strat)) {
  codes <- as.character(1:11)
  ar <- as.character(strat$admission_reason)
  ind <- t(vapply(ar, function(s) {
    if (is.na(s)) return(setNames(rep(NA_integer_, length(codes)), codes))
    setNames(as.integer(codes %in% parse_reasons(s)), codes)
  }, integer(length(codes))))
  ind <- ind[stats::complete.cases(ind), , drop = FALSE]
  colnames(ind) <- codes

  cat("Patients used for co-occurrence: ", nrow(ind), "\n", sep = "")
  prev <- tibble::tibble(code = codes, patients = as.integer(colSums(ind)))
  save_tab(prev, "tab46_13_admission_reason_prevalence",
           caption = "Prevalence of each admission-reason code.")

  cooc <- crossprod(ind)
  phi  <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor(ind))

  phi_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(phi))
  names(phi_long) <- c("code_i", "code_j", "phi")
  phi_long$code_i <- factor(phi_long$code_i, levels = codes)
  phi_long$code_j <- factor(phi_long$code_j, levels = rev(codes))

  p_phi <- ggplot(phi_long, aes(code_i, code_j, fill = phi)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(phi), "", sprintf("%.2f", phi))),
              size = 2.6) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1a6faf", mid = "white", high = "#d73027",
                         midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), na.value = "grey85",
                         name = "phi") +
    labs(title = "Admission-reason co-occurrence",
         subtitle = "Binary correlation; phi > 0 means the two reasons appear together more than chance.",
         x = "Code", y = "Code") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8))
  print(p_phi)
  save_fig(p_phi, "fig46_18_admission_reason_phi", width = 7, height = 6)

  cooc_long <- as.data.frame(as.table(cooc))
  names(cooc_long) <- c("code_i", "code_j", "n")
  cooc_long$code_i <- factor(cooc_long$code_i, levels = codes)
  cooc_long$code_j <- factor(cooc_long$code_j, levels = rev(codes))

  p_cooc <- ggplot(cooc_long, aes(code_i, code_j, fill = n)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(n) | n == 0, "", n)), size = 2.6) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "#fde0d9", high = "#c0392b", na.value = "grey85",
                        name = "Patients") +
    labs(title = "Admission-reason co-occurrence counts",
         subtitle = "Cell = patients carrying both reasons; the diagonal is the prevalence.",
         x = "Code", y = "Code") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 8))
  print(p_cooc)
  save_fig(p_cooc, "fig46_19_admission_reason_cooccurrence", width = 7, height = 6)
}
```

# 7. Manifest of generated artefacts

Every figure and table written by this run, for cross-checking against

```{r manifest}
# The artefact name encodes its destination: tab4S_nn / fig4S_nn belongs to
# Chapter 4 Section 4.S. The manifest makes that mapping explicit.
section_of <- function(f) {
  m <- regmatches(basename(f), regexpr("^(tab|fig)4[1-6]", basename(f)))
  if (length(m) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  paste0("4.", substr(m, 5, 5))
}

figs <- tibble::tibble(file = list.files(FIG_DIR, full.names = TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(section = vapply(file, section_of, character(1)),
                kb = round(file.info(file)$size / 1024, 1)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(file)
tabs <- tibble::tibble(file = list.files(TAB_DIR, full.names = TRUE)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(section = vapply(file, section_of, character(1)),
                kb = round(file.info(file)$size / 1024, 1)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(file)

print(knitr::kable(figs, caption = "Figures written by this run."))
print(knitr::kable(tabs, caption = "Tables written by this run."))

cat("\nFigures: ", nrow(figs), " files (PNG + PDF pairs). Tables: ",
    nrow(tabs), " CSV files.\n", sep = "")
```
